articles.headline: Americans vote in midterm elections serving as referendum on Trump
articles.title: U.S. votes for midterm elections, seen as referendum on Trump
articles.summary: Citizens across the United States cast ballots on Tuesday in congressional elections deciding control of the House of Representatives and Senate during the final two years of President Donald Trump's second term. The nationwide vote encompasses all 435 House seats, 37 Senate seats, and numerous gubernatorial races. Pre-poll forecasts suggest the Democratic Party could capture the House, potentially constraining the administration's policy agenda.
articles.description: The polling will decide whether President Trump’s Republican Party retains control of the House of Representatives and the Senate, the two chambers of the U.S. Congress, or, as opinion polls are predicting, the Democratic Party wrests control of at least the House if not the Senate, also in the final two years of Mr. Trump’s second term in office

articles.headline: US launches limited military strikes on Iran ahead of midterm elections
articles.title: US strikes Iran ahead of midterm elections
articles.summary: United States forces launched limited military strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, according to officials speaking to CBS. Iranian state news agency IRNA reported explosions following the operation, which President Donald Trump described as a response to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps firing on an aircraft. The developments occur ahead of congressional elections that will determine party control of the United States legislature.
articles.description: US officials described the attacks on Qeshm Island as limited and defensive, according to CBS, the BBC's US partner.

articles.headline: Supreme Court declines Trump request to halt California vote count
articles.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump's request to stop California counting disputed votes
articles.summary: The United States Supreme Court issued a one-line order on Monday denying a justice department request to set aside 20,000 mail-in ballots in California. Federal authorities had alleged the votes may have been issued to non-citizens, a claim questioned by state election officials who cited inaccuracies in the government lists. The ruling allows lower court decisions to stand on the eve of midterm elections determining congressional control.
articles.description: The ruling, which comes on the eve of the midterm elections, essentially ends the Trump administration's bid to disqualify the ballots in the state.

articles.headline: Multiple Russian strikes kill at least 26 at Ukraine aid centre
articles.title: Multiple Russian strikes kill at least 26 at Ukraine aid centre
articles.description: At least 26 people were killed in Russian strikes on a school being used as a humanitarian aid centre.

articles.headline: Republicans scramble in final push ahead of midterm elections
articles.title: Trump's Republicans scramble to stop Democratic midterms wave
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump and Republican candidates made a final push on November 1, 2026, ahead of November 3 midterm elections where Democrats are projected to take control of the House. According to NBC News, 60 percent of Americans disapprove of Trump's performance amid inflation and an eight-month conflict with Iran. Campaigns saw roughly 11 billion dollars spent on advertising, with heavy donations from figures like Elon Musk. High-stakes contests and early voting by 54 million citizens reflect intense national political division.
articles.description: While Tuesday is election day, early voting has already seen a record 54 million people cast ballots around the country, reflecting the intense political fervour

articles.headline: Severe cyclone Murasu approaches Andhra Pradesh coast for landfall
articles.title: Severe Cyclone Murasu: Landfall commences near Ongole
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department reported that severe cyclonic storm Murasu is approaching the coastline of Andhra Pradesh near Ongole. Landfall is expected before three in the morning on November 3, 2026. The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority issued warnings for extremely heavy rainfall across multiple mandals in Prakasam district, amid gales reaching up to one hundred kilometers per hour.
articles.description: The landfall is happening close to Ongole, with gale-force winds of 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph; he same wind speed is likely to prevail till morning along and off the coast near the landfall point.

articles.headline: Democrats threaten Republican control of the US Senate ahead of midterm elections
articles.title: Republicans defend their bastions, as senate comes within reach of Democrats
articles.summary: As the United States approaches midterm elections, forecasts indicate that the Republican Party majority in the Senate is under threat from Democrats. The party currently holds a 53 to 47 majority with thirty-five seats contested this year, including seven toss-up seats identified by the Cook Political Report across several states according to reports published on October twenty-ninth, 2026.
articles.description: The GOP has a 53–47 majority in the Senate currently, with 35 seats being contested this year. Of these, seven are “toss ups”, according to a non-partisan election analyser. These seats are in Iowa, Arkansas, Kansas, Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Texas. All of these – except Michigan – are seats which are currently held by Republicans

articles.headline: Russian air defenses intercept numerous drones following conclusion of regional truce
articles.title: Russia downs hundreds of drones after Ukraine truce ends
articles.summary: Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin reported that Russian air defenses intercepted nearly 500 drones targeting the capital on November 3, 2026. The escalation followed the expiration of a Kherson region truce on November 1. Concurrently, strikes across Ukraine killed 26 people, triggered Polish air defenses, and disrupted regional medical and critical infrastructure as U.S.-led talks loom.
articles.description: The attacks followed a rare pause in the fighting between Russia and Ukraine in the southern Ukrainian region of Kherson, which ended November 1

articles.headline: Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia village kill 26 people following truce expiration
articles.title: Russia-Ukraine war: Strikes on a school by Russia kills 26, derailing hopes of progress toward peace
articles.summary: Ukrainian officials stated that Russian strikes on a Zaporizhzhia village school distributing humanitarian aid killed at least 26 people on November 2, 2026. The attack followed the expiry of a Kherson ceasefire brokered by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump. Acting regional Governor Mykhailo Semikin confirmed casualties included rescuers and police officers as U.S.-led talks approach.
articles.description: Russia resumed its strikes on the southern region of Kherson after the end of a ceasefire in the area, the longest truce in the war raging between the neighbours since Russia’s 2022 invasion, Kyiv said

articles.headline: Former Maldives foreign minister Abdulla Shahid arrested on abuse charges
articles.title: Former Maldives Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid arrested on child sexual abuse charges
articles.summary: Police in the Maldives arrested former Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid late Monday following a court order concerning child sexual abuse allegations. Local media reported that the prominent opposition politician has denied the charges. The arrest holds significance as the former United Nations General Assembly president is a presidential aspirant for the Maldivian Democratic Party in the upcoming elections.
articles.description: The arrest assumes significance as Mr. Shahid is among the prominent presidential aspirants within the main opposition Maldivian Democratic Party (MDP) for the island nation’s 2028 elections

articles.headline: Texas Senate candidates Paxton and Talarico make final appeals
articles.title: Texas Senate candidates Paxton and Talarico make final appeals
articles.description: Texas Senate candidates Ken Paxton (R) and James Talarico (D) made their last appearances before Tuesday’s election.

articles.headline: Israeli military attacks across Gaza leave multiple Palestinians dead and injured
articles.title: Israeli forces kill four in Gaza as fifth Palestinian dies of wounds
articles.summary: Medical sources and media reports stated that Israeli forces killed at least four Palestinians in attacks across Gaza, while a fifth person died from previous wounds. The Palestinian Ministry of Health reported that ongoing operations have killed at least 74,609 people. Meanwhile, Board of Peace high representative Nickolay Mladenov arrived in Israel to discuss reconstruction and winter shelter.
articles.description: Nearly 1,600 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since a US-brokered 'ceasefire' took effect in October last year.

articles.headline: US midterms test Republican redistricting strategies in Texas and beyond
articles.title: US midterms present a test for Republican redistricting in Texas and beyond
articles.summary: Republican state legislatures implemented rare mid-decade redistricting in Texas and other states ahead of midterm elections to secure potential congressional gains. Critics argue the new boundaries dilute minority voting power by altering traditional districts, while defenders maintain the changes reflect shifting voter trends. Approximately thirty-five million voters nationwide are casting ballots within newly redrawn political boundaries for this election cycle.
articles.description: Partisan redistricting has transformed elections for Black voters in Houston as Democrats seek new pathways to victory.

articles.headline: Delhi air quality plunges to very poor category as stage two GRAP invoked
articles.title: Air quality of Delhi slips to ‘very poor’ for first time this winter, Stage 2 of GRAP invoked
articles.summary: Air quality in the national capital deteriorated sharply, prompting the implementation of Stage-II of the Graded Response Action Plan across the National Capital Region on Monday. The air quality index reached 324, driven by unfavourable meteorological conditions according to forecasts from the India Meteorological Department. Authorities directed regional governments to increase parking fees and stagger office timings to curb rising pollution levels.
articles.description: AQI of Delhi stood at 324 (very poor) at 4 p.m. on November 2, up from 261 (poor) a day earlier; NCR State governments to enhance vehicle parking fees to discourage use of private vehicles, staggered timings to be introduced for public offices and municipal bodies; Delhi Metro to run 20 more trips on weekdays

articles.headline: Israeli forces arrest Al Jazeera correspondent Montaser Nassar in West Bank
articles.title: Israeli forces release Al Jazeera journalist in occupied West Bank
articles.summary: Israeli soldiers detained Al Jazeera Arabic correspondent Montaser Nassar during a raid on his home in Dura, near Hebron, on Tuesday. Video footage showed him blindfolded and handcuffed before being led into a military vehicle alongside at least 12 other Palestinians. According to sources, all detainees were taken to an undisclosed location following the operation in the occupied West Bank.
articles.description: Video of the arrest shows Israeli forces leading Montaser Nassar, who was blindfolded and handcuffed, into a vehicle.

articles.headline: Delhi air quality remains very poor with severe pollution in parts
articles.title: Parts of Delhi reel under ‘severe’ level air pollution
articles.summary: Delhi maintained a very poor air quality category on November 3, 2026, with specific areas like Rohini, Punjabi Bagh, and Narela recording severe pollution levels. According to Central Pollution Control Board data, the 24-hour average Air Quality Index reached 330 at 8 a.m. Meteorological factors and seasonal stubble burning continue to worsen regional air conditions across northern India.
articles.description: The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 330 (very poor) at 8 a.m. on November 3, 2026, as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data

articles.headline: Israeli soldiers arrest Al Jazeera journalist in Hebron raids
articles.title: Israeli soldiers arrest Al Jazeera journalist in Hebron raids
articles.description: Israeli soldiers blindfolded, handcuffed and arrested Al Jazeera correspondent Montaser Nassar during a raid on his home

articles.headline: United States military carries out defensive strikes against Iranian targets in Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: U.S. has conducted defensive strikes on some Iranian targets in Strait of Hormuz: official ahead of midterm elections
articles.summary: American forces executed limited defensive strikes on Monday, November 2, 2026, targeting Iranian assets utilizing surface-to-air missiles near Qeshm Island. The operation occurred ahead of United States midterm elections, as Vice-President J.D. Vance expressed optimism regarding potential negotiated settlements. Meanwhile, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly lobbied for continued military action to aid domestic political objectives.
articles.description: Vice-President J.D. Vance told reporters that he just spoke to President Trump about talks with Iran and said that “the president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement”

articles.headline: Trump administration plans to remove South Africa and Rwanda from trade agreement
articles.title: Trump to remove Rwanda and South Africa from US trade deal
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump notified Congress of his plan to exclude South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act beginning January 1, 2027. United States Trade Representative Jamieson Greer stated that annual reviews revealed both countries engaged in practices violating program requirements. Washington cited trade barriers, security concerns, and human rights issues as the primary reasons for the upcoming terminations.
articles.description: The move comes barely a week after Rwanda's defence ministry was hit with sanctions by the US Treasury.

articles.headline: Supreme Court declines administration request to segregate thousands of California mail ballots
articles.title: U.S. Supreme Court rejects Trump administration push to set aside thousands of California ballots
articles.summary: The Supreme Court declined on Monday, November 2, 2026, to intervene in a Republican administration request to set aside approximately 20,000 mail ballots in California flagged as potential non-citizens. Lower courts warned that segregating the documents before Tuesday midterm elections would disenfranchise legal voters and create severe logistical disruptions. Department of Justice attorneys acknowledged substantial error rates within their tracking data during the proceedings.
articles.description: Another federal judge ruled against the administration's efforts to make last-minute demands of California election officials, finding they violated the Constitution

articles.headline: United States encourages Venezuela to pursue phased democratic transition following high-level meeting
articles.title: US urges Venezuela to follow phased plan for democratic transition
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Venezuelan Minister of Foreign Affairs Oliver Blanco on Monday to discuss a phased plan involving stabilization, economic recovery, and political reconciliation. The diplomatic engagement follows last year's abduction of former President Nicolas Maduro and recent oil agreements granting North American Blue Energy Partners significant extraction rights. Opposition leader Maria Corina Machado recently returned to organize upcoming electoral movements.
articles.description: This comes as leading opposition leader returns to Venezuela and hints at criticism of Trump administration.

articles.headline: Explosions rattle Qeshm Island as reports indicate American military action in Hormuz
articles.title: Explosions hit Iran’s Qeshm Island as US media report US strikes in Hormuz
articles.summary: Explosions occurred on Iran's Qeshm Island and in Bandar Lengeh on Monday, coinciding with reports from American media outlets that United States forces conducted defensive strikes in the Strait of Hormuz. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for capturing two reconnaissance drones and destroying an MQ-9 drone. President Donald Trump subsequently minimized conflict prospects on social media ahead of Tuesday midterm elections.
articles.description: Several explosions heard on Qeshm Island and in Bandar Lengeh as US media report US military strikes in Hormuz.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh sounds alert as severe cyclonic storm Murasu approaches coast
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu nears A.P. coast, heavy rain alert issued
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government issued alerts across five districts as severe cyclonic storm Murasu approached for landfall between Ongole and Nellore on November 2, 2026. The India Meteorological Department warned of very heavy rainfall and wind speeds reaching up to 120 kmph. Authorities deployed National Disaster Response Force teams, arranged electricity poles, and dispatched rescue personnel to manage potential disruptions.
articles.description: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the storm is likely to move with a “wind speed of 100 to 110 kmph (and) gusting up to 120 kmph between Nellore and Narasapur”.

articles.headline: Thousands displaced as homes are bulldozed in India’s Assam state
articles.title: Thousands displaced as homes are bulldozed in India’s Assam state
articles.description: Hundreds of homes have been bulldozed in the Dhubri district of Assam state in northeastern India.

articles.headline: Russian airstrikes on Komyshuvakha aid centre kill 24 people
articles.title: Russian bombing kills 26 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
articles.summary: At least 24 people were killed after Russian aerial bombs struck a humanitarian aid distribution centre located inside a school in the southern Zaporizhzhia region village of Komyshuvakha. According to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and regional head Mykhailo Semikin, the attack injured five people and left 27 missing. Rescue operations were repeatedly halted due to ongoing drone activity.
articles.description: Officials say at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit a southern Ukrainian village in what the president called an "utterly horrific" attack.

articles.headline: United States strikes Qeshm Island amid ongoing regional tensions and diplomatic discussions
articles.title: U.S. strikes Iran's Qeshm Island: report
articles.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported on Monday, November 2, 2026, that the United States military executed strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island following explosions noted by state media agency IRNA. The operation represents a continuation of limited, undisclosed actions distinct from full-scale military campaigns. President Donald Trump stated that a diplomatic agreement with Tehran remains possible and denied plans for post-election strikes.
articles.description: The Wall Street Journal added that strikes have been carried out on ‌a smaller scale and purposefully ​kept secret so as not to signal any intent ⁠of resuming its major military campaign against Iran

articles.headline: Maria Corina Machado returns to Venezuela after months in exile
articles.title: Venezuela's Opposition leader Machado returns after months in exile, as doubts over democracy deepen
articles.summary: Opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returned to Venezuela from exile on October 25, 2026, arriving in Lara to greet supporters. Her return follows the U.S. military ouster of former President Nicolas Maduro and acting President Delcy Rodriguez taking power. Machado and her allies have demanded a presidential election date, while U.S. officials emphasize prior economic stabilization.
articles.description: Acting President Delcy Rodriguez was initially supposed to serve only 90 days as acting president, but has remained in office and has made no move to call an election

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi challenges Prime Minister Narendra Modi to open debate
articles.title: Rahul Gandhi challenges PM Modi to open debate on ‘foreign help’
articles.summary: Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to an open debate following accusations that the opposition relies on foreign assistance to destabilise the country. Gandhi alleged on social media that Modi owes his position to foreign backing and financial support. Modi had previously criticized the opposition in Gujarat for obstructing national development and spreading rumors.
articles.description: Congress leader alleges that it was with ‘foreign help’ that Modi became PM; this comes after the Prime Minister accused the Opposition of taking foreign help to destabilise the country

articles.headline: Trump makes final midterms pitch at Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool
articles.title: Trump makes final midterms pitch at Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool
articles.description: US President Donald Trump urged supporters to turn out ahead of Election Day

articles.headline: Iranian negotiators continue talks in Doha to end U.S.-Iran war
articles.title: Iranian negotiators in Doha to continue talks to end the U.S.-Iran war, official says
articles.summary: Iranian delegates met with Qatari mediators in Doha on November 1, 2026, for a third consecutive day of discussions to end the ongoing conflict. According to an official, the talks are coordinated with Washington as officials navigate diplomatic efforts amidst concerns of regional escalation following upcoming U.S. midterm elections, while Tehran's military remains on high alert.
articles.description: The talks come amid concerns that the conflict ‌could escalate again after the November 3 U.S. midterm elections

articles.headline: PM Modi credits renewable energy investments for softening West Asia crisis impact
articles.title: Clean energy investments helped India soften West Asia crisis impact: PM Modi
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated on November 2, 2026, that prior investments in renewable energy helped cushion India from the worst impacts of the West Asia crisis. Speaking at an expo in New Delhi, Modi projected $220 billion in investment opportunities for the sector by the end of the decade and highlighted the rapid expansion of domestic solar module manufacturing.
articles.description: Inaugurating Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo, Narendra Modi says India’s economy continued to grow despite the crisis; warns that excess dependence on fossil fuels could risk increased exposure to global disruptions

articles.headline: Ebola outbreak death toll surpasses 5,300 across multiple nations
articles.title: Ebola outbreak kills more than 5,300 people in DR Congo
articles.summary: According to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, the death toll from the ongoing Ebola outbreak has exceeded 5,300 fatalities. The Democratic Republic of the Congo remains the epicentre of the health crisis, with additional cases and deaths reported in Uganda, Kenya, Nigeria, and France involving the rare Bundibugyo strain of the virus.
articles.description: The Bundibugyo strain has spread to Kenya and Uganda, while two in Nigeria returned negative results.

articles.headline: Binance restores customer withdrawals following record cryptocurrency theft
articles.title: Binance restarts withdrawals after $6.3bn heist
articles.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance resumed withdrawals in stages on Sunday after hackers stole approximately 6.3 billion dollars in digital assets last week. The company stated it has replaced about 95 percent of the affected funds and will absorb the financial loss. Meanwhile, the Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed the security breach to North Korea.
articles.description: The FBI says hackers from North Korea are responsible for the theft.

articles.headline: Delhi authorities demolish settlements around historic mosque and relocate families
articles.title: 'We grew up around this historic Delhi mosque - now we have been forced out'
articles.summary: Authorities in Delhi demolished hundreds of homes across three settlements on October 7, relocating 717 families to Savda Ghevra on the city outskirts due to security concerns and illegal land usage. While the centuries-old mosque remains standing without water and electricity, the Delhi High Court scheduled a hearing for December 16 to address ongoing legal petitions regarding access and preservation.
articles.description: Authorities have razed hundreds of houses in a neighbourhood in central Delhi, saying they were built on government land.

articles.headline: Small jet crashes in Florida neighbourhood, killing all nine people on board
articles.title: Plane may have broken apart ahead of deadly Florida jet crash, say investigators
articles.summary: A business jet traveling from Austin to the Bahamas crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people on board. The Learjet 60 plummeted into a residential street on Sunday at approximately 12:50 EST, causing a massive explosion and damaging local infrastructure. According to the United States transport secretary, the Federal Aviation Administration is assisting a National Transportation Safety Board investigation into the tragedy.
articles.description: The National Transportation Safety Board also believes weather could have been a factor in the crash, but warns it is too early to determine the cause.

articles.headline: European nations rehearse potential military deployment to Ukraine
articles.title: Thousands of European troops to rehearse Ukraine deployment in event of peace
articles.summary: Britain and France are leading a multinational military exercise in Poland involving nearly 3,000 personnel from 12 European nations. The training aims to test deployment capabilities for a potential reassurance force in Ukraine once peace is achieved, though Western officials stress the troops will not engage in offensive operations or act under NATO command.
articles.description: Western officials stress that any force sent to Ukraine would not take part in any offensive operations.

articles.headline: Asia-Pacific nations watch United States midterms amid economic strain
articles.title: War, tariffs and China: What the US midterms mean for the Asia-Pacific
articles.summary: Governments and businesses across the Asia-Pacific region are closely monitoring United States midterm elections following severe energy shortages and tariffs. Analysts note that while regional leaders hope for significant policy shifts regarding trade and the war on Iran, a divided United States Congress is unlikely to alter presidential decisions.
articles.description: Hit hard by Trump's tariffs and the war on Iran, countries in the Asia-Pacific want 'enormous changes' in US policies.

articles.headline: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio meets Venezuelan counterpart in Washington
articles.title: Rubio meets Venezuelan counterpart as U.S. presses for progress on election preparations
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio held discussions with Venezuelan Foreign Minister Oliver Blanco in Washington to advance preparations for upcoming elections. The diplomatic engagement follows a recent electoral reform blueprint agreed upon by local authorities and opposition figures, as the administration of President Donald Trump continues monitoring political developments after the ouster of former leader Nicolás Maduro.
articles.description: The meeting held on November 2 was one of the highest-level encounters between a senior Trump administration official and a counterpart from acting President Delcy Rodríguez's government

articles.headline: President Donald Trump faces low approval ratings ahead of midterm elections
articles.title: Trump approval rating near record low on eve of US midterm elections: Poll
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump approaches the midterm elections with a job approval rating lingering near historical lows, according to recent polling data. While the president campaigned extensively to support Republican candidates trying to maintain congressional control, surveys indicate widespread voter dissatisfaction driven by economic concerns and inflation following regional conflicts.
articles.description: Only 32 percent of voters approve of Trump's job performance in the latest Reuters/Ipsos poll.

articles.headline: Darius Khambata criticises Tata Sons chairman reappointment decision
articles.title: Chandra’s reappointment has sullied Tata Sons’ image: Darius Khambata
articles.summary: Outgoing Tata Trusts board member Darius Khambata has resigned, stating that the decision to grant N. Chandrasekaran a third term as Tata Sons chairman has damaged the company's reputation. Khambata expressed his concerns in a letter to Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata, highlighting internal divisions regarding share listings and fiduciary duties.
articles.description: ‘The sad events of September 17, 2026, a day that will live in infamy, have sullied Tata Sons’ reputation and imperilled the image of corporate India. No amount of spin doctoring can mask what happened,’ said the outgoing Tata Trusts board member

articles.headline: Voters prioritize economy and cost of living ahead of U.S. midterms
articles.title: US midterms 2026: What polls reveal about Democratic, Republican voters
articles.summary: Voters across the United States head to the polls as surveys highlight deep divisions over economic conditions, personal finances, and key policy issues between Democrats and Republicans. While economic concerns remain paramount for both parties, voters diverge significantly regarding the importance of healthcare, immigration, and trust in leadership during the current congressional midterm elections.
articles.description: From the economy and cost of living to immigration, polls suggest where American voters agree and disagree.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh deploys disaster response teams ahead of Cyclone Murasu
articles.title: Cyclonic storm Murasu to make landfall close to Ongole
articles.summary: Authorities in Andhra Pradesh have deployed six National Disaster Response Force teams and seven State Disaster Response Force teams across vulnerable districts as Cyclone Murasu approaches. According to the India Meteorological Department, the storm is expected to make landfall near Ongole with wind speeds up to 120 kilometers per hour in the early hours of November 3, 2026.
articles.description: NDRF, SDRF teams deployed in districts likely to be affected

articles.headline: United States to suspend South Africa and Rwanda from trade pact
articles.title: US to suspend South Africa and Rwanda from duty-free trade access
articles.summary: The United States announced it will remove South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act duty-free trade programme starting January 1, 2027. United States Trade Representative Jamieson Greer stated that both nations failed to meet eligibility criteria regarding governance and trade barriers. South Africa exported about one point seven billion dollars in goods under the scheme in 2025.
articles.description: South Africa to lose duty-free access, affecting $1.7bn worth of annual exports, including cars and farm products.

articles.headline: Israeli prime minister pushes for military strikes against Iran
articles.title: Netanyahu pressing Trump to attack Iran after midterms, says officials
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is urging United States President Donald Trump to launch air strikes against Iran following the November midterm elections. Regional officials report the push aims to help form an emergency government after coalition losses. Meanwhile, Qatari mediators are pursuing diplomatic talks to halt attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for lifting port blockades.
articles.description: A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Benjamin Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week's elections

articles.headline: Amit Shah defends voter list revisions during Hyderabad political event
articles.title: Amit Shah backs SIR, alleges 3 crore ‘illegal infiltrators’ identified in 13 crore deleted voters
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah claimed on November 2, 2026, that the Election Commission of India removed three crore illegal infiltrators from Bangladesh during the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Speaking in Hyderabad, he criticized opposition leaders for opposing the exercise and challenged Rahul Gandhi to a parliamentary debate regarding voter list integrity.

articles.headline: United States administration petitions Supreme Court to block California ballots
articles.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump request to set aside California ballots
articles.summary: The administration of United States President Donald Trump filed an emergency request with the Supreme Court to halt California from counting mail-in ballots from over twenty thousand alleged non-citizens. The Department of Justice argues these votes must be isolated until citizenship is verified, while California officials contend the list is unreliable and disenfranchises legitimate voters. Lower federal courts previously rejected the administration requests.
articles.description: Top court declines to block California from counting ballots of voters Trump administration claims are not US citizens.

articles.headline: Iran accelerates ceasefire proposal for US negotiations
articles.title: Trump signals progress on Iran deal as Tehran pushes faster ceasefire
articles.summary: Iranian officials stated on Monday that their seven-step ceasefire proposal submitted to the United States has been condensed for faster implementation within two days. The plan involves reopening the Strait of Hormuz and resuming nuclear talks. Discussions are ongoing with Qatari mediators, while US President Donald Trump indicated potential military action following the November 3 midterm elections if a deal is not reached.
articles.description: Iran says its offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz can be implemented in two days if the US agrees to terms.

articles.headline: Madras High Court criticises police over political case filings
articles.title: Police must serve the State, which endures, and not the party in government, which changes: Madras High Court
articles.summary: The Madras High Court disapproved of police registering criminal cases against critics of the ruling party while granting anticipatory bail to Greater Chennai Corporation Councillor D. Sudha. Justice N. Ramesh stated that police serve the enduring State rather than changing governments. The judge also criticised the unauthorised dawn detention of Madras Institute of Development Studies Associate Professor A. Kalaiyarasan over a fake Instagram account.
articles.description: The observations were made while granting anticipatory bail to a 60-year-old Councillor, D. Sudha of the DMK, who had allegedly abused Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay

articles.headline: Russian bomb attacks on Ukrainian aid centre kill 24 people
articles.title: Russian bombing of Ukrainian aid centre kills 26 people
articles.summary: Russian air strikes destroyed a school serving as a humanitarian aid center in Komyshuvakha within Ukraine's Zaporizhia region, killing 24 people. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that a repeat strike hit a shelter where residents had gathered. Regional Governor Mykhailo Semikin confirmed that casualties included two emergency rescuers and a police officer, with 27 individuals reported missing following Monday's bombardment.
articles.description: Ukraine's president calls attack further proof that Russia does not want any ‌kind of de-escalation or real justice.

articles.headline: The New York Times sues Brave browser for copyright infringement
articles.title: The New York Times sues Brave web browser for AI scraping and bypassing paywalls
articles.summary: The New York Times, alongside the New York Daily News, the Chicago Tribune, and the Orlando Sentinel, filed lawsuits against Brave Software. The publishers accuse the web browser of unlawfully scraping copyrighted material to train artificial intelligence models and allowing users to bypass publication paywalls without permission or compensation, according to legal complaints.
articles.description: The New York Times and a group of other publications have filed lawsuits against the company that makes the Brave web browser over alleged unlawful scraping to train AI and also letting users bypass their paywalls, as reported by Reuters. According to a complaint filed by the New York Daily News, the Chicago Tribune, and […]

articles.headline: Fighting resumes in Ukraine after temporary truce near Kherson region
articles.title: Fighting returns to Kherson region after longest Ukraine war ceasefire
articles.summary: Hostilities resumed in Ukraine's Kherson region on November 2, 2026, following a six-day ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump. Local authorities reported fresh Russian strikes, including a hit on a medical facility in Kherson city. While the truce enabled hundreds of civilians to evacuate from Oleshky, both sides utilized the pause for military regrouping.
articles.description: Though unprecedented, the six-day truce has done little to alter the wider trajectory of a war that continues to grinds on.

articles.headline: US political candidates conduct final campaign events ahead of midterms
articles.title: Trump, Vance campaign with candidates on last day before US midterms
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance held final campaign events on November 3, 2026, ahead of the midterm elections. Republicans sought to defend congressional majorities against strong Democratic challenges driven by economic and foreign policy concerns, while a federal court reviewed a lawsuit regarding immigration agents at polling places.
articles.description: President Donald Trump closes his midterm campaign push at the Reflecting Pool, urging supporters to vote.

articles.headline: Iran offers to reopen Hormuz strait within two days if US agrees
articles.title: Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if U.S. agrees to demands
articles.summary: Tehran announced readiness to reopen the strategic Strait of Hormuz within forty-eight hours if Washington accepts specific conditions, including lifting oil sanctions and ending military actions. Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei stated on November 2, 2026, that messages are being exchanged through mediators while U.S. President Donald Trump simultaneously issued renewed threats during election campaigning.
articles.description: A senior Iranian official said the offer to open the vital energy corridor, which follows intense efforts by mediators to stop a return to war, showed good faith

articles.headline: Supreme Court orders time-bound financial aid and rehabilitation for freed bonded labourers
articles.title: Supreme Court orders time-bound financial aid, rehabilitation for rescued bonded labourers
articles.summary: The Supreme Court directed the Centre on November 2, 2026, to ensure financial assistance is disbursed to rescued bonded labourers within seven days of release. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh instructed States and Union Territories to implement a revised standard operating procedure within six months, aiming to eradicate institutional shortcomings, strengthen inter-state coordination, and secure meaningful rehabilitation.
articles.description: Bench says eradication of bonded labour is a “continuing obligation”, requiring authorities to ensure that those freed are meaningfully rehabilitated

articles.headline: Odisha government expedites evacuation of vulnerable areas as Cyclone Murasu approaches
articles.title: Odisha braces for severe cyclonic storm Murasu, evacuates 1.6 lakh people
articles.summary: The Odisha government accelerated evacuations from vulnerable areas on Monday as Cyclone Murasu strengthened into a severe storm in the Bay of Bengal. Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari stated that over 300 rescue teams have been pre-positioned across southern districts like Ganjam and Gajapati, where the India Meteorological Department forecast heavy rainfall and gusty winds reaching up to 50 kmph.
articles.description: The State government’s preparedness efforts are focused on the five districts of Ganjam, Gajapati, Malkangiri, Koraput, and Kandhamal

articles.headline: Business jet crash in Florida claims lives of nine people
articles.title: Jet crashes into South Florida neighbourhood, killing all nine on board and leaving a fiery crater
articles.summary: A Learjet 60 business jet crashed into a residential neighborhood in South Florida on November 1, 2026, resulting in the deaths of all nine individuals on board, according to United States Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy. The aircraft, bearing tail number N722BD, had departed from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was traveling toward the Bahamas before plunging near Military Trail and 10th Avenue North.
articles.description: The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration

articles.headline: Israeli strikes kill three Palestinians in Gaza Strip, health officials report
articles.title: Israeli strikes kill three people in Gaza, medics say
articles.summary: Israeli airstrikes killed at least three Palestinians and wounded several others across the Gaza Strip on November 2, 2026, according to territory health officials. Medics reported two deaths in Khan Younis and one in Al-Mussadar. The Israeli military stated the strikes targeted militants, while ongoing conflict and stalled ceasefire negotiations continue to affect more than two million residents.
articles.description: Medics said two people were ⁠killed and six others wounded in two separate airstrikes in Khan Younis while ‌a third person was killed in an Israeli airstrike in the town of ‌Al-Mussadar

articles.headline: China ramps up Middle East diplomacy with high-level meetings involving Iran and Oman
articles.title: China steps up Middle East diplomacy with Iran and Oman meetings
articles.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with an Iranian security official in Beijing on November 2, 2026, while President Xi Jinping hosted Oman’s Sultan Haitham bin Tariq. Beijing renewed calls for dialogue regarding the conflict and signed fourteen cooperation documents with Oman. Officials emphasized the importance of safeguarding energy routes and called for the resumption of safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.description: Beijing urges dialogue on US-Iran war, sends envoy to Gulf as Xi hosts first Omani head of state visit since 1978.

articles.headline: WHO warns northern Ethiopian conflict threatens health system with collapse
articles.title: Violence in northern Ethiopia pushing health system towards collapse: WHO
articles.summary: Escalating fighting and drone strikes in northern Ethiopia are driving the regional medical infrastructure toward total collapse, according to World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. Speaking on November 2, 2026, Tedros reported that recent violence has killed multiple civilians, including children in the Amhara region, while severe shortages of staff, medicine, and ambulances hinder life-saving care.
articles.description: Renewed fighting between rebels from northern Tigray and ​the government in Addis Ababa has shattered 2022 peace deal.

articles.headline: Government issues new rules allowing airfare intervention in extraordinary situations
articles.title: Centre can intervene on airfares in ‘extraordinary’ circumstances, new rules say
articles.summary: Under newly framed rules notified on October 31, the Union government can now issue written directions to airlines regarding ticket prices during extraordinary situations. The regulations require carriers to submit tariffs to the Director General of Civil Aviation and publish detailed cost breakdowns on digital platforms. While providing for enhanced price monitoring, authorities maintained that base fares remain market-driven without direct caps.
articles.description: Centre has previously imposed fare bands during the pandemic, IndiGo’s operational breakdown, and urged restraint during disasters, festivities; new rules also mandate closer monitoring of fares by DGCA

articles.headline: Amit Shah challenges Rahul Gandhi to debate parliamentary session on electoral rolls
articles.title: Amit Shah dares Rahul Gandhi to debate SIR issue, says government is ready to convene special session of Parliament
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah challenged Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to a debate during a special session of Parliament on Monday. Dismissing opposition allegations regarding electronic voting machines and voter rolls, Shah asserted that the government is fully prepared to convene the House. He also strongly criticized opposition rallies and vowed that authorities would systematically remove every infiltrator from electoral rolls.
articles.description: If a Parliament session is held, Prime Minister Narendra Modi will shred Congress into pieces, Amit Shah said

articles.headline: Al Jazeera condemns extension of Israeli operational ban and calls for immediate lifting
articles.title: Al Jazeera condemns Israeli ban extension, calls for its immediate lifting
articles.summary: The Qatar-based Al Jazeera Media Network strongly condemned the Tel Aviv court decision approving a ninety-day extension of its operational ban in Israel. Calling the measure an assault on press freedom, the organization rejected allegations used to justify the restrictions and criticized the lack of due process regarding secret material. The network announced it is reviewing the ruling with legal counsel to protect its journalists and public access to information.
articles.description: Network calls move 'assault' on press freedom, warns of 'dangerous pattern' that undermines ability to report facts.

articles.headline: US oil firms earn over $130bn in profits during war on Iran
articles.title: How US oil firms profit $130bn from Iran war as household bills surge
articles.summary: United States oil companies earned more than 130 billion dollars in profits during the war on Iran, according to The New York Times, while consumers faced soaring costs. Brown University reported that Americans spent an extra 150 billion dollars on petrol and diesel. Analysts warned that high energy prices could risk economic growth and potential recession while increasing shareholder returns.
articles.description: As energy from the Gulf and Russia take a hit, American oil and gas firms are the big gainers.

articles.headline: Israel's policy aims to minimize Palestinian population, says UN official
articles.title: Israel’s intent is to prevent Palestinians from existing as a group: Justice Muralidhar
articles.summary: Israel implements policies to maximize the occupation of Palestinian territories and minimize the Palestinian population, according to Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar. Speaking on a podcast, the chair of the UN-appointed Independent International Commission of Inquiry stated the commission demonstrated Israel's intent to prevent Palestinians from existing as a group while gathering evidence of war crimes in occupied territories.
articles.description: In a strong indictment of Israel’s policies in the occupied Palestinian territories, Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, chair of the UN-appointed Independent International Commission of Inquiry, has accused Israel of seeking to expand its occupation while reducing the Palestinian population

articles.headline: Iran military warns third conflict with US and Israel will be costly
articles.title: How would Tehran respond if the US and Israel bomb Iran again?
articles.summary: Iran military officials warned that a renewed war with the United States and Israel would be longer and more costly than expected, utilizing new weapons and asymmetric warfare. Former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander Hossein Kanani Moghaddam said Iranian forces are in better operational shape, while analysts noted ongoing domestic security concerns and intelligence weaknesses within the regime.
articles.description: Iran has retained significant offensive capability, but civilians and critical infrastructure remain largely exposed.

articles.headline: Iran says US talks could resume ‘within a short period’ if demands are met
articles.title: Iran says US talks could resume ‘within a short period’ if demands are met
articles.description: Esmaeil Baghaei said Qatar is facilitating indirect talks based on Iran’s seven-step peace plan.

articles.headline: India manufacturing sector activity growth eases in October amid softer output and new orders
articles.title: Manufacturing PMI eases to 54.7 in October, but overseas demand at six-month high
articles.summary: India's manufacturing sector growth slowed in October as output and new orders increased at milder rates, according to the HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index compiled by S&P Global. The seasonally adjusted index fell to 54.7 from 55.1 in September. HSBC Chief India Economist Pranjul Bhandari noted that strong international demand pushed new export orders to a six-month high while input cost inflation retreated to its lowest level since February.
articles.description: Even as demand increased, the survey respondents said that cost pressures eased in October

articles.headline: China urges political solutions to resolve conflict in West Asia
articles.title: West Asia conflict: China's Foreign Minister pushes for dialogue
articles.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi stated on November 2, 2026, that all parties in the West Asia conflict should prioritize political solutions rather than armed conflict. Speaking in Beijing with Ali Bagheri Kani of Iran, Mr. Wang emphasized negotiation. Additionally, Chinese President Xi Jinping told Omani leader Sultan Haitham bin Tariq al-Said that the region should not become a battleground for great-power rivalry.
articles.description: Dialogue ‌and negotiation are the way ‌to ⁠resolve West Asia conflicts, Chinese FM ⁠told Ali Bagheri Kani, the Deputy Secretary of the Iran Supreme National Security Council

articles.headline: Iran considers two-day plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Iran says considering two-day plan to reopen Hormuz
articles.summary: Iran announced on November 2, 2026, that it is evaluating a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the United States accepts specific demands, including ending the West Asia war, lifting oil sanctions, and unfreezing assets. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei stated that messages are being exchanged via mediators, while U.S. and Israeli officials continue to issue military threats.
articles.description: “The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran's good-faith approach,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said

articles.headline: Sudan files formal complaints against Ethiopia over drone attacks
articles.title: Sudan files complaints against Ethiopia with UN over deadly drone spree
articles.summary: Sudan lodged complaints with the United Nations Security Council and the African Union regarding deadly drone attacks originating from Ethiopian territory. The Sudanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs accused the Rapid Support Forces of using Ethiopian bases to target civilian sites. A report from the Transitional Sovereignty Council stated that 70 assaults since February 2026 resulted in hundreds of casualties.
articles.description: One-way drone attacks have killed or wounded 484 civilians since February, Khartoum says.

articles.headline: Displaced Sudanese families struggle amid worsening food shortages and famine
articles.title: As aid situation worsens, displaced Sudanese worry about warnings of famine
articles.summary: Displaced Sudanese citizens across camps face severe food insecurity and declining humanitarian aid as the conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces and Rapid Support Forces continues. Aisha Adam, who fled to Port Sudan, works daily to buy basic supplies. Meanwhile, the World Food Programme and the United States Department of State warned of a rising famine risk affecting millions nationwide.
articles.description: Sudan's displaced people now face a mounting food crisis, with warnings of famine.

articles.headline: Scientists react as artificial intelligence disrupts foundational computer science hypotheses
articles.title: Shock and regret: scientists react to AI roiling life’s work
articles.summary: OpenAI and Anthropic announced that artificial intelligence models disproved the exponential time hypothesis, which posits that certain computational problems require exhaustive answers. Originators Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi, and researcher Ryan Williams are organizing an independent review. The developments have sparked academic debate regarding the future of human research, tool accessibility, and the rapid pace of technological change.
articles.description: OpenAI and Anthropic each said last week that one of their AI models had disproved the exponential time hypothesis

articles.headline: What are Americans voting for in this election?
articles.title: What are Americans voting for in this election?
articles.description: The BBC's Maddie Gerber explains what's on the ballot in the 2026 midterm elections in the United States.

articles.title: Trump makes controversial claims at final Republican campaign rallies
articles.description: Donald Trump made a series of provocative remarks during his final Republican campaign rallies.

articles.headline: North coastal Andhra Pradesh records early rainfall from approaching Cyclone Murasu
articles.title: Rain begins in north Andhra ahead of Cyclone Murasu
articles.summary: North coastal Andhra Pradesh received initial rainfall on Monday from severe cyclonic storm Murasu moving from the Bay of Bengal. Kakinada Rural mandal recorded 51.75 mm of rain between 8.30 a.m. and noon, according to data from the Andhra Pradesh Directorate of Economics and Statistics. The India Meteorological Department expects landfall between Monday night and Tuesday morning near Ongole, with officials warning the damage depends on storm strength.
articles.description: Kakinada (Rural) mandal records 51.75 mm by noon; the storm is likely to cross the coast near Ongole tonight

articles.headline: Why ISRO’s latest success matters more than it appears | The Hindu Editorial
articles.title: Why ISRO’s latest success matters more than it appears | The Hindu Editorial
articles.description: The successful GSLV-F18 mission could restore NavIC’s capabilities and strengthen India’s independent navigation system. But experts say bigger reforms, more funding and greater manufacturing capacity will be needed if India wants to achieve its long-term space ambitions.

articles.headline: India evacuates thousands as Cyclone Murasu approaches Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: Thousands evacuated as India braces for second cyclone in a week
articles.summary: Authorities in Andhra Pradesh began moving residents from low-lying coastal areas as Cyclone Murasu approached the region on November 2, 2026. Prakhar Jain of the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority stated that about 2,000 individuals had been relocated by Monday, with plans to reach 30,000. The India Meteorological Department projected wind speeds of up to 110 kilometres per hour, threatening power supplies and infrastructure across multiple districts.
articles.description: Cyclone Murasu expected to hit near Ongole late Monday with wind speeds of 100-110km/h, Meteorological Department says.

articles.headline: United Nations demands independent investigation into human rights worker's death in Houthi custody
articles.title: UN staffer’s death in custody exposes Houthi ‘political extortion’ in Yemen
articles.summary: The United Nations is demanding a transparent investigation into the death of Mohammad el-Shami, a human rights employee who died in Houthi detention in Yemen. UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk urged authorities in Sanaa to disclose medical records and preserve evidence. El-Shami was arbitrarily detained in June 2024 among dozens of targeted personnel, making him the second UN staff member to die in custody.
articles.description: Following a UN staffer's death, rights experts expose systematic abuses and demand international accountability in Yemen

articles.headline: Binance customers withdraw billions in assets following major cryptocurrency hack
articles.title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after largest-ever crypto hack
articles.summary: Binance users withdrew 3.6 billion dollars on November 1, 2026, as the cryptocurrency exchange reopened following a massive cyberattack impacting 6.3 billion dollars in digital assets. The Federal Bureau of Investigation and other organisations attributed the breach to North Korea. Binance stated that it has covered approximately 95 percent of the stolen funds using corporate reserves and insurance funds.
articles.description: The exchange froze transactions following the incident which has been linked to a North Korean group.

articles.headline: The unending purge in Xi’s China
articles.title: The unending purge in Xi’s China
articles.description: China’s Fifth Plenum confirmed the expulsion of 33 Central Committee members, including 16 Generals, signalling that Xi Jinping’s anti-corruption purge is far from over; the purge has raised questions about PLA leadership and combat readiness, while Xi’s succession plans remain unclear ahead of the 2027 Party Congress

articles.headline: Hormuz shipping still faces major risks
articles.title: Hormuz shipping still faces major risks
articles.description: The Strait of Hormuz remains dangerous and costly for shipping, despite US claims that it is open.

articles.headline: Indian political consultants deploy shadow social media campaigns to influence foreign elections
articles.title: Shadowy Indian election ‘consultants’ add US midterms to global footprint
articles.summary: Specialised private companies based in India are operating coordinated online influence networks to manipulate international elections, including the United States midterms and Kenya's presidential race. According to researchers, these firms use anonymous accounts, premium virtual private networks, and altered content on platforms like Meta and Google to evade regulatory standards and avoid public scrutiny.
articles.description: India's election consultants are exporting covert campaign tactics to manipulate elections worldwide, including the US.

articles.headline: Israeli forces withdraw from Hebron after ten-day military siege
articles.title: Hebron governor says Israeli forces withdraw from city after 10-day siege
articles.summary: Palestinian security forces have assumed control of Hebron following the departure of Israeli troops who concluded a ten-day military operation. Governor Khaled Dudin confirmed that displaced residents could return home. The siege, initiated after an October 23 shooting attack that killed two Israeli soldiers, resulted in significant property destruction, infrastructure damage, and the displacement of more than 3,300 people.
articles.description: Hebron Mayor Youssef al-Jaabari says families forced from their homes can return and students can go to school.

articles.headline: Protesters clash with security forces in Manipur following recovery of bodies
articles.title: Agitators clash with security forces in Manipur's Kangpokpi after recovery of missing youths' bodies
articles.summary: Demonstrators clashed with security personnel in the Kangpokpi district of Manipur on November 2, 2026, after the mutilated remains of two missing youths were discovered in Senapati. Law enforcement deployed tear gas and baton-charged the crowd to disperse stone-throwing agitators. Local officials and community leaders strongly condemned the violence while demanding an independent and transparent investigation into the killings.
articles.description: Protests erupted in several parts of Kangpokpi district on November 1, as agitators burned tyres on many roads and blocked several stretches with logs of wood and boulders

articles.headline: 'I couldn't be silent': Iranian teen's mother seeking justice after daughter shot dead
articles.title: 'I couldn't be silent': Iranian teen's mother seeking justice after daughter shot dead
articles.description: BBC Panorama follows grieving Samira who - after the killing of Sevda - faces up to the Tehran regime.

articles.headline: Mother fights Iranian regime after security forces kill teenage daughter
articles.title: Iran killed her teenage daughter - now she is facing up to the regime
articles.summary: Samira fled Iran on foot and went into hiding abroad after her sixteen-year-old daughter Sevda was shot dead by security forces during anti-government protests on January 9, 2026. According to the mother, authorities hindered her search for the body and forced her to blame terrorists for the death. While human rights groups estimate thousands of fatalities, the Iranian embassy claimed protests were hijacked by foreign powers.
articles.description: Samira's 16-year-old daughter Sevda was shot dead as they took part in mass protests in January.

articles.headline: North Indian cities record very poor air quality levels
articles.title: Air quality worsens to ‘very poor’ category in Delhi, parts of north India
articles.summary: The overall air quality in Delhi and several north Indian cities deteriorated to the very poor category on November 2, 2026, according to official data. The Central Pollution Control Board reported that Delhi recorded a 24-hour average Air Quality Index of 310 at 8 a.m. The Central government warns that hazardous pollution levels will persist for up to six days, driven by meteorological conditions, vehicle emissions, dust, stubble burning, and post-festive firecrackers.
articles.description: The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 310 (very poor) at 8 a.m. on November 2, 2026, as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data

articles.title: Bulgaria has its first elected female president
articles.description: Iliana Iotova has won Bulgaria’s presidential runoff, becoming the country’s first elected female president.

articles.headline: Trump repeats unverified claims during final midterm campaign rallies
articles.title: Trump leans into Islamophobia and conspiracy in last-ditch campaign rallies
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump delivered his final travelling campaign speeches on November 1, 2026, in Iowa and Kansas, urging supporters to vote in the upcoming November 3 midterms. Trump repeated unfounded claims regarding Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, calling him a jihadist and a member of the Muslim Brotherhood. The rallies also featured attacks on other Democratic figures, discussions of the US-Israel war on Iran, and immigration concerns as polls indicate potential Democratic gains in both states.
articles.description: Trump attacks Muslim politicians Abdul El-Sayed and Ilhan Omar in his two last rallies on the campaign trail.

articles.headline: Donald Trump holds final weekend rallies across key states ahead of elections
articles.title: Trump makes final campaign push in final weekend before election
articles.summary: Donald Trump campaigned in Florida, Iowa, and Kansas over the weekend to rally support and protect Republican majorities in Congress ahead of Tuesday's midterm elections. Facing voter frustration over rising living costs, the president shifted his focus to attacking Democrats. Meanwhile, forecasting tools and national polls suggest Democrats hold a strong advantage in capturing control of the legislative branch.
articles.description: The US president rallied in states that Republicans previously won - showcasing how tight Tuesday's elections could be in determining control of Congress.

articles.headline: Independent voters surge as record spending defines midterms
articles.title: US midterms: What to know about independent voters and candidates
articles.summary: Nearly half of United States adults identify as politically independent ahead of the November 3, 2026, midterms, according to the Pew Research Center. Despite this demographic shift, independent candidates face severe financial barriers in an electoral cycle projected to surpass billions in ad spending. While major parties dominate, pollsters note that independent voters could prove decisive in determining the balance of power in Congress and state legislatures.
articles.description: Despite a record number of independents, third-party candidates and voters struggle to penetrate the two-party system.

articles.headline: Kimi Antonelli becomes Formula One's youngest world champion
articles.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes Formula One’s youngest world champion in Mexico City
articles.summary: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli secured third place at the Mexico City Grand Prix on November 1, 2026, to become Formula One's youngest world champion at 20 years and 68 days old. Red Bull driver Max Verstappen won the red-flagged race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, while Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton finished second. Antonelli's historic victory makes him the first Italian champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953, pushing his overall lead to an unassailable 119 points.
articles.description: Italian wonderkid wins drivers' championship at 20 years and 68 days, finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

articles.headline: Venezuelan army attack on Colombian rebel camp leaves 19 dead
articles.title: At least 19 dead in Venezuela army attack on Colombian rebel camp
articles.summary: At least 19 people were killed during a Venezuelan military attack on a National Liberation Army camp in the western state of Apure, according to an NGO and a military source. The operation, which took place on October 30, 2026, targeted the Colombian guerrilla group with drone and helicopter strikes supported by United States intelligence.
articles.description: Juan Francisco Garcia, a coordinator with the group, said on November 1 that “Ten bodies” had been transported to the state capital, San Fernando, the day after the attack

articles.headline: Kimi Antonelli secures Formula 1 world championship in Mexico
articles.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion; Max Verstappen wins in Mexico
articles.summary: Italian driver Kimi Antonelli secured his maiden Formula 1 world championship on November 2, 2026, at the Mexico City Grand Prix after finishing third behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton. At 20 years and 68 days old, the Mercedes driver surpassed Sebastian Vettel as the youngest champion in the sport's history, while Verstappen claimed victory in the race with a time of 2 hours, 20 minutes and 28.772 seconds.
articles.description: Antonelli ‌celebrated his first F1 world championship at 20 years and 68 ‌days old, ⁠more than three years younger than Germany’s Sebastian Vettel when ⁠he set the previous record in 2010

articles.headline: Cyber attacks strike Russia and Ukraine following truce conclusion
articles.title: Cyber attacks hit Russia, Ukraine after truce ends
articles.summary: Russia reported a massive cyber attack on its public emergency warnings application on November 2, 2026, hours after Ukraine suspected similar hostile interference in its air raid alert system. The digital disruptions occurred as the longest truce of the conflict, which was limited to the Kherson region and brokered by United States First Lady Melania Trump, officially concluded on November 1, 2026, following Russian refusal to extend the pause.
articles.description: The cyber attacks came as the longest truce of the war, limited to Ukraine’s eastern Kherson region, ended on November 1, 2026 after Russia refused the offer of an extension, according to Kyiv

articles.headline: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva stages political turnaround in Brazil election
articles.title: Brazil elections | Historic win, humongous challenges
articles.summary: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva staged a remarkable political turnaround after trailing Flavio Bolsonaro by 45.2 to 47 percent at the end of the first round of Brazil presidential elections, which saw an abstention rate of 21 percent. Thousands of students and workers subsequently marched across urban centers like Niteroi and Rio de Janeiro in widespread protests against Bolsonarism, marking the return of the Left to the streets after more than a decade.
articles.description: Lula tweaked his campaign’s message, speaking more about reducing working hours, relief for indebted families and higher welfare payments under the Bolsa Familia scheme

articles.headline: Thousands gather at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi for INDIA bloc rally
articles.title: ‘You can break a stick, not a bundle’: Thousands turn up for INDIA bloc rally from across the country
articles.summary: Supporters from across India arrived in Delhi on November 1, 2026, to attend the opposition INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan. Attendees voiced concerns over electoral roll revisions, healthcare, and education. Leaders alleged that authorities attempted to block travel, while participants sought political change and revival ahead of upcoming elections.
articles.description: Citizens, youth groups, farmers and political party workers gather ahead of the Ramlila Maidan rally, saying a united movement is needed to fight alleged vote theft and electoral roll irregularities

articles.headline: Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge attacks Prime Minister Narendra Modi at rally
articles.title: ‘Remove Modi to save democracy’: Congress chief Kharge attacks PM at INDIA bloc rally
articles.summary: Indian National Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge alleged on November 1, 2026, that Bharatiya Janata Party governments at the Centre and in multiple states were formed on stolen mandates. Speaking at an opposition INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi, Kharge accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah of shielding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to disenfranchise marginalized citizens.
articles.description: Addressing INDIA bloc's rally at Ramlila Maidan on the "vote chori" charge, Mr. Kharge also accused Prime Minister Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah of shielding Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar

articles.headline: Israeli election results stand despite Netanyahu voter fraud claims
articles.title: Israeli officials say results stand as Netanyahu claims election ‘stolen’
articles.summary: Israel's Central Elections Committee head Noam Sohlberg stated that general election results will remain valid despite foreign interference claims. Prime Minister Benyamin Netanyahu accused Arab-led parties of stealing the vote with Qatari funding. Meanwhile, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot alleged Netanyahu is attempting to delegitimise the outcome, while President Isaac Herzog prepares to nominate a government leader.
articles.description: Election body says deadlocked result won't be undermined even if foreign interference claims are found to be true.

articles.headline: French prosecutors launch attempted murder probe over petrol bomb attack
articles.title: France launches attempted murder investigation after petrol bomb thrown at police
articles.summary: French prosecutors initiated an attempted murder investigation after incendiary devices were thrown at police during demonstrations in Paris. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez condemned the attack, which injured fifteen officers, including one with severe burns. Authorities recorded over seven hundred arrests during nationwide youth-led protests over the weekend concerning the high cost of living.
articles.description: There were hundreds of arrests as protesters took to the streets in cities across France for the third weekend in a row.

articles.headline: Marc Marquez claims Malaysian MotoGP victory to near world title
articles.title: Marquez wins in Malaysia to stand on brink of MotoGP world title
articles.summary: Ducati star Marc Marquez secured a dominant victory at the Malaysian MotoGP in Sepang, finishing ahead of Pedro Acosta and Alex Marquez. The thirty-three-year-old Spaniard expanded his championship lead to forty-four points over Jorge Martin, who missed the race with a wrist injury. Marquez can clinch his eighth world title at the upcoming event in Qatar.
articles.description: Marquez, who is now 44 points ahead of his closest rival Jorge Martin, has seven victories to his name this season

articles.headline: Kherson truce ends after evacuation of civilians from Oleshky
articles.title: Kherson braces for return of war as localised Russia-Ukraine truce ends
articles.summary: A six-day localized ceasefire in Ukraine's Kherson region expired without extension or violations on Sunday night, following a joint evacuation operation that relocated hundreds of civilians from Oleshky. According to Ukrainian and Russian officials, ongoing strikes continued across multiple regions, leaving hundreds of thousands of households without power and causing casualties, including a fatal drone attack in Vinnytsia.
articles.description: Moscow and Kyiv continue strikes elsewhere, but no reported violations in Kherson region during the six-day ceasefire.

articles.headline: Israeli strike kills Palestinian schoolboy in Deir el-Balah
articles.title: Education under fire: Gaza’s children face death on their way to school
articles.summary: Fourteen-year-old Mohammed Hamad was killed by an Israeli strike on October 17 while walking home from school in the al-Baraka neighbourhood of Deir el-Balah with his younger brother Abdullah. According to the Gaza Ministry of Health, escalating violence near the Yellow Line has resulted in numerous child casualties and school disruptions, leaving surviving students like injured fourth-grader Suad Abd Rabbo in urgent need of overseas medical treatment.
articles.description: Children have faced Israeli bombs and sniper fire since the academic year resumed in Gaza.

articles.headline: Russian strikes cut power across Ukraine as Kherson evacuation truce ends
articles.title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends
articles.summary: Russian strikes on energy infrastructure across four regions left hundreds of thousands of homes without power as a humanitarian ceasefire in the Kherson region expired on Sunday night. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky reported extensive damage and ongoing repairs. Meanwhile, a separate strike in the Vinnytsia region killed two people, and Ukraine retaliated by hitting a missile fuel producer in Russia's Rostov region.
articles.description: A rare humanitarian ceasefire allowed civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.

articles.headline: Thousands displaced from Hebron as Israel carries on siege
articles.title: Thousands displaced from Hebron as Israel carries on siege
articles.description: Almost 5,000 people have been displaced as a result of Israel’s military siege on the city of Hebron in the West Bank.

articles.headline: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney discusses trade future with Donald Trump
articles.title: Canada PM Carney says he had good conversation with Trump on trade
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced on Sunday that he held discussions with United States President Donald Trump regarding future bilateral trade arrangements. Writing on the social media platform X, Carney stated that negotiating teams will work in the coming weeks to deliver a mutually beneficial agreement following months of escalating tariffs between the two neighboring countries.
articles.description: Canada and the United States have ⁠slapped billions of dollars in tariffs on each other in ‌recent months

articles.headline: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney signals progress in United States trade discussions
articles.title: Carney signals progress on Canada-US trade deal talks as midterms loom
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced positive progress toward a future trade agreement with the United States on Sunday, just two days prior to the United States midterm elections. Bilateral ties have experienced significant strain due to billions of dollars in mutual tariffs enacted during an escalating trade war between the two North American nations.
articles.description: Canadian PM Mark Carney announces progress in Canada-US trade deal talks ahead of Tuesday's US midterm elections.

articles.headline: Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova leads presidential runoff exit polls
articles.title: Bulgarian President wins runoff election: exit polls
articles.summary: Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova is projected to win Sunday's presidential runoff vote, according to exit polls showing her receiving between 50.7 and 52.5 percent. The election occurred amidst security concerns in European Union and North Atlantic Treaty Organization member states following recent drone attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea. Iotova faces Andrey Gyurov, a banker backed by the pro-Western opposition.
articles.description: The vote took place amid security concerns in the EU and NATO member states following a series of drone attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea

articles.headline: Acting President Iliana Iotova leads exit polls in Bulgaria runoff
articles.title: Initial results indicate victory for Iotova in Bulgarian presidential vote
articles.summary: Bulgaria acting President Iliana Iotova led the presidential election runoff with just over half the vote on Sunday, according to three exit polls reported by the Bulgarian Telegraph Agency. The election took place while twenty-one people remained missing following Black Sea drone attacks last month. Iotova competed against Andrey Gyurov, a banker and former caretaker prime minister who criticized her stance on Russia.
articles.description: Acting President Iotova would become nation’s first elected female head of state if official results confirm her win.

articles.headline: Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu discuss Iran war strategy on call
articles.title: Trump holds call with Netanyahu over state of Iran war: report
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu discussed ongoing negotiations and military strategy regarding Iran during a phone call on Saturday, according to media reports citing American and Israeli officials.
