articles.summary: OpenAI announced on Monday that it will pilot its Grid Protectors Program at a planned data center in Effingham County, Georgia. The company stated the initiative will free up to 1,000 megawatts of electricity during extreme weather to support local homes. The strategy aims to address growing public and legislative backlash across the United States regarding the immense energy demands of artificial intelligence infrastructure.
articles.description: In an announcement on Monday, OpenAI says it will pilot its "Grid Protectors Program" at an upcoming data center in Effingham County, Georgia, where the company promises to free up to 1,000 megawatts of power during extreme weather or emergencies, enough to power air conditioners in around 700,000 homes. The announcement comes as opposition to […]

articles.headline: Manisha Bhanwala wins India’s first women’s wrestling world title in Astana
articles.title: Manisha Bhanwala: The 29-year-old who ended India’s wait for a women’s wrestling world title
articles.summary: Wrestler Manisha Bhanwala secured a historic gold medal in the 59kg freestyle category at the World Wrestling Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan, defeating American competitor Abigail Nette on October 31, 2026. This victory marks India's first-ever women's world title in the sport. The 29-year-old athlete from Jind, Haryana, dedicated her triumph to her late father Suresh Bhanwala, capping an unprecedented campaign that also featured silver medals from teammates Neelam Sirohi and Kajal Dhochak.
articles.description: From a village in Haryana to the pinnacle of international wrestling, Manisha Bhanwala scripted history in Kazakhstan, becoming India’s first woman world champion

articles.headline: Supermarket freezers across seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
articles.title: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
articles.summary: Dozens of supermarkets across seven European countries suffered refrigerator and freezer malfunctions caused by a suspected cyber-attack that forced evaporator settings into defrost mode. Stores in Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia, and Finland reported spoiled produce and rising temperatures. Sabcobel CEO Stephan Moelans stated that affected units were disconnected from networks while national cybersecurity agencies monitored the ongoing situation.
articles.description: The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C.

articles.headline: 'All this food is now useless': Piles of rubbish after shop freezers hit by cyber-attack
articles.title: 'All this food is now useless': Piles of rubbish after shop freezers hit by cyber-attack
articles.description: Dozens of supermarkets in seven European countries dumped huge quantities of food after refrigerators and freezers were targeted in a cyber-attack.

articles.headline: Arab citizens surge to polls in high-turnout Israeli election
articles.title: Ra’am and Joint List | The surge of the other
articles.summary: Israel recorded a high voter turnout of seventy-seven percent during its recent general election, driven by an overwhelming mobilization among Arab citizens. The Joint List and the United Arab List secured a combined nineteen seats in parliament. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu criticized the surge, while Arab leaders sought representation against policies they argue perpetuate discrimination.
articles.description: Israel’s Arab parties made historic gains in elections but uncertainty remains whether the opposition bloc would join hands with them to form a government

articles.headline: Three Aam Aadmi Party MLAs join Bharatiya Janata Party in Punjab
articles.title: Three AAP leaders join BJP ahead of Punjab Assembly election
articles.summary: Three Aam Aadmi Party legislators, including Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Chetan Singh Jauramajra, joined the Bharatiya Janata Party at headquarters in New Delhi on November 2, 2026. Two of the quitting politicians cited unfulfilled promises from the 2022 polls. The ruling Aam Aadmi Party criticised the Bharatiya Janata Party for inducting leaders facing serious allegations.
articles.description: Amritsar North MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap, Sanour MLA Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Samana MLA Chetan Singh Jauramajra join the BJP in Delhi; State BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon says it indicates the impending end of the party’s regime in Punjab

articles.headline: Scientists use epigenetic control to silence hepatitis B viral DNA
articles.title: Gene therapy offers to beat hepatitis B virus by muting its DNA
articles.summary: Researchers have developed an experimental therapy called CRMA-1001 that successfully silences hepatitis B virus DNA in mice by selectively adding methylation marks without altering host genes. According to a study published on September 21 in Nature Biomedical Engineering, the technique utilizes CRISPR-Cas9 to deliver the silencing machinery, offering a promising path toward a lasting functional cure by preventing viral rebound.
articles.description: An experimental therapy called CRMA-1001 is a remarkable development because, instead of targeting the virus directly, it silences the viral DNA; this is promising because current treatments rarely eliminate the DNA, which allows the virus to rebound

articles.headline: Dutch authorities offer record reward for fugitive drug lord Jos Leijdekkers
articles.title: Dutch police offer record €2m reward in hunt for drug lord
articles.summary: Dutch authorities announced a record reward of two million euros on Monday for information leading to the arrest of Jos Leijdekkers. Justice Minister David van Weel emphasized the threat posed by the fugitive, who was previously convicted in absentia in Rotterdam and Belgium for drug smuggling and money laundering. Europol lists Leijdekkers among Europe's most-wanted suspects.
articles.description: Jos Leijdekkers has been found guilty in absentia of cocaine smuggling and is believed to be in Sierra Leone.

articles.headline: Drone strikes target multiple electricity substations across eastern and northern Sudan
articles.title: Drone attacks extend campaign targeting Sudan’s power system
articles.summary: Drone strikes hit three electricity substations in New Halfa, Aroma, and Northern State on Monday, causing widespread power outages. Local media reports indicate this brings the total number of attacks on Sudan's electricity network to 18 within a week. Sudan's military government accused Ethiopia of assisting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces in targeting civilian infrastructure.
articles.description: Attacks the latest to disrupt electricity supplies; army reports new defections from paramilitary RSF.

articles.headline: Village defence guard and wife found dead from bullet wounds in Reasi
articles.title: Village guard, wife die of bullet wounds in Jammu’s Reasi
articles.summary: Javed Ahmed, a village defence guard, and his wife Shaheen Akhter were found dead from bullet wounds in Jammu and Kashmir's Reasi district on November 2, 2026. Initial reports suggested the shots were fired from a government-issued service weapon. Separately, an Army porter was injured by an anti-personnel mine near the Line of Control in Rajouri district.
articles.description: This is the third such incident in the past two years in the Jammu region

articles.headline: India thrashes Korea to finish league phase of Asian Champions Trophy
articles.title: Asian Champions Trophy: India ends league phase with a thumping win over Korea
articles.summary: The Indian men's hockey team defeated Korea 8-0 on November 2, 2026, finishing the league stage of the Asian Champions Trophy with complete domination and an undefeated run. Dilpreet Singh scored twice in the match held ahead of the upcoming semifinals. In another fixture, Japan defeated Malaysia 2-1 to secure second place in the tournament standings.
articles.description: The two teams will meet again in Wednesday’s semifinal while Japan takes on Malaysia in the other last-four clash

articles.headline: New study explores how smoking sets the stage for lung cancer
articles.title: How smoking sets the stage for lung cancer, glimpsed in new study
articles.summary: This article is a partial text or introduction that outlines a scientific conundrum regarding how chronic inflammation from smoking damages lung tissue and increases cancer risk long before definitive mutations take root, without providing further details or study outcomes.
articles.description: Chronic smoke exposure alters lung stem cells and weakens their safety mechanisms and local immune defences, creating a precancerous state; common KRAS and TP53 mutations triggered tumours only in smoke-conditioned tissue, showing how smoking primes cells for cancer

articles.headline: Foreign secretary Vikram Misri to visit Nepal for bilateral talks
articles.title: In first high-level visit after new government’s arrival, Foreign Secretary Misri to visit Nepal on November 4-5
articles.summary: Ministry of External Affairs announced that Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri will visit Kathmandu on November 4 and 5, 2026. The high-level visit follows Prime Minister Balendra Shah taking charge in March. Discussions will cover bilateral cooperation and former Indian Army soldiers protested in Kathmandu demanding resumed Gurkha recruitment under the Agnipath scheme.
articles.description: Misri’s visit to include discussions on Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit to India; appointment of Nepal’s new Ambassador to India and disaster assistance following the flash floods are also expected to be on the agenda

articles.headline: Congress demands Joint Parliamentary Committee probe into IDBI Bank sale
articles.title: Congress seeks JPC probe into IDBI Bank sale, alleges valuation irregularities
articles.summary: The Congress party demanded an immediate halt and a Joint Parliamentary Committee investigation into the proposed sale of IDBI Bank to Canada-based Fairfax Financial Holdings. Senior leader Shaktisinh Gohil alleged valuation manipulations and transparency issues in the government's October 14 approval to divest a majority stake for approximately 53,000 crore rupees.
articles.description: The party questions the use of bank’s funds by Fairfax to finance acquisition; demands disclosure of valuation reports

articles.headline: Enterprise analytics report highlights poor quality and context issues in AI agents
articles.title: Raising the quality of insights in agentic analytics
articles.summary: A sponsored report by MIT Technology Review's Insights and Snowflake reveals that fewer than half of agent-generated insights lead to business improvement due to insufficient context and fragmented data. While generative AI expands analytics access, 52 percent of surveyed organizations face insight overload, prompting companies to prioritize data governance and semantic layers to improve performance.
articles.description: In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to users across the organization. Agentic AI promises to do even more, by automating entire workflows and taking actions based on agent insights. But there is a problem: The quality of insights that agents currently generate…

articles.headline: H.D. Kumaraswamy dares Bengaluru police to take action against him
articles.title: Nobody has the guts, says HDK, dares police to take action against him
articles.summary: Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy challenged the Bengaluru City Police to arrest him on November 2, 2026, while denying allegations that a controversial sting video targeting former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah was exchanged at his Delhi home. Accusing Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar of conspiring with the accused, Kumaraswamy questioned the objectivity of the ongoing Central Crime Branch investigation.
articles.description: Kumaraswamy accuses Shivakumar of conspiring to distribute ‘sleaze’ videos of Prajwal Revanna; he accuses the Bengaluru Police Commissioner of acting at the behest of the Chief Minister and questions the objectivity of the probe in the sting video case

articles.headline: Karnataka invites Japanese businesses to build technology and manufacturing partnerships
articles.title: Bring your technology; we’ll provide talent, land and partnerships, Karnataka tells Japanese business delegation
articles.summary: The Karnataka government urged Japanese enterprises to leverage the State's industrial ecosystem, skilled talent pool, and supportive policies during the India-Japan Business Summit 2026. Principal Secretary S. Selvakumar emphasized local strengths in electronics and aerospace manufacturing on November 2, 2026, while trade bodies signed agreements to train engineering students in Japanese language skills.

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Israel’s lockdown of Hebron comes to an end
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Israel’s lockdown of Hebron comes to an end
articles.description: Israeli forces ended their lockdown of Hebron in the occupied West Bank, but its forces continued to attack a school.

articles.headline: Congress reviews election preparedness for Uttarakhand and Manipur assemblies
articles.title: Congress reviews poll preparedness in Uttarakhand, Manipur; targets BJP governments
articles.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge led high-level meetings on November 2, 2026, with party leaders from Uttarakhand and Manipur to evaluate organizational readiness for upcoming assembly polls. Attendees discussed electoral strategies alongside criticisms of Bharatiya Janata Party governance, citing prolonged ethnic conflict in Manipur and deteriorating law enforcement in Uttarakhand.
articles.description: After meeting Congress leaders from Uttarakhand, party chief Mallikarjun Kharge accuses the BJP’s ‘double engine’ government of betraying the hopes and aspirations of the people over its 10 years in power in the State

articles.headline: Parliament panel to discuss helicopter safety following Uttarakhand crash
articles.title: Parliament panel to meet on Uttarakhand helicopter crash
articles.summary: The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture scheduled a meeting for November 13 with aviation officials to review helicopter safety. The panel, led by Janata Dal-United Member of Parliament Sanjay Jha, aims to examine frequent crashes in Uttarakhand, including a recent incident on October 30 that resulted in six fatalities near Joshimath.
articles.description: The panel is also expected to deliberate on the high number of helicopter crashes that were reported from Uttarakhand in 2025

articles.headline: U.K. Defence Minister warns EU against protectionist policies in Brussels
articles.title: U.K. warns EU against keeping Britain out of ‘Made in Europe’
articles.summary: United Kingdom Defence Minister Wes Streeting cautioned the European Union on November 2 against potential protectionism in its industrial strategy. Speaking ahead of a Brussels summit scheduled for November 20 with Prime Minister Andy Burnham and European officials, Streeting expressed concern that British industries might face exclusion from the Made in Europe initiative.
articles.description: The European Union wants to boost domestic sectors like cars and defence by forcing companies to buy European if they want public money

articles.headline: Karnataka Rakshana Vedike begins state-wide campaign to collect IT employment data
articles.title: Despite CM’s appeal, KRV begins State-wide drive to seek hiring data from IT firms
articles.summary: The Karnataka Rakshana Vedike launched a month-long state-wide campaign to request recruitment details from information technology and biotechnology companies regarding local hiring practices. Led by state president T.A. Narayanagowda, members visited nearly fifty companies on November 2, 2026, despite an appeal from Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to avoid direct visits while the government examines discrimination allegations.

articles.headline: India will maintain capital expenditure to support economic growth, Sitharaman says
articles.title: Capex push to continue, but fiscal prudence non-negotiable: FM
articles.summary: Union Finance and Corporate Affairs Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated on Monday in Mumbai that the Indian government will sustain its capital expenditure push to secure economic growth. Speaking at an HSBC India event, she emphasized that fiscal prudence remains a top priority and that public investment multipliers have proven successful over the past four to five years.
articles.description: “India must to talk with optimism and there needs to be reduction in cynicism says Ms. Sitaraman

articles.headline: Japan urges US military discipline following second Marine arrest in Okinawa
articles.title: Japan urges U.S. to enforce discipline after second Marine arrest
articles.summary: Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi announced on Monday that Tokyo has requested the United States strictly enforce troop discipline. The appeal follows the recent arrest of a Marine on suspicion of drunk driving during a curfew, coming shortly after another serviceman was indicted for murder in Okinawa.
articles.description: The case has triggered outrage in Japan and reignited controversy over the heavy U.S. military presence on the southern island

articles.headline: At least seven migrants die on boat bound for Canary Islands amid storm
articles.title: At least seven migrants die on boat bound for Canary Islands amid storm
articles.description: At least seven migrants have died aboard a boat carrying 139 people bound for the Canary Islands after a storm hit.

articles.headline: Birla Estates targets residential expansion and tenfold commercial rental growth
articles.title: Birla Estates eyes top-three spot, targets 10-fold jump in office rentals
articles.summary: Real estate developer Birla Estates plans to expand its residential portfolio across major cities while aiming for a tenfold increase in annual commercial rental income to fifteen hundred crore rupees over four to five years. Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer K.T. Jithendran stated that residential demand remains strong, particularly in Bengaluru where market growth outperformed other urban regions.
articles.description: There is no sign of slowness in the market as both pricing and absorption remain extremely steady and positive, says K.T. Jithendran, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Birla Estates

articles.headline: Kimi Antonelli becomes Formula One's youngest champion in Mexico City
articles.title: Antonelli’s coronation could well be the change of guard
articles.summary: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli secured his maiden Formula One driver championship after finishing third in the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The twenty-year-old Italian became the sport's youngest titleholder by surpassing Sebastian Vettel. Team boss Toto Wolff gambled on the rookie to replace Lewis Hamilton, and Antonelli capitalized with a five-race winning streak and a historic victory in Monza.
articles.description: It was fitting that he was joined on the rostrum by Verstappen (winner) and Hamilton (second), the two drivers who have been the icons of Formula One for the last 15 years

articles.headline: Maine lobster industry faces economic strain from tariffs and trade tensions
articles.title: Lobster industry caught in Maine’s political headwinds before US midterms
articles.summary: Commercial fishermen in Maine are grappling with rising operational costs and trade uncertainties ahead of the United States midterm elections. President Donald Trump's tariffs on Canadian goods and subsequent retaliatory measures have disrupted supply chains where a significant portion of the catch is processed across the border.
articles.description: Senator Susan Collins and Democratic challenger Troy Jackson clash over tariffs and their impact on Maine's economy.

articles.headline: Hebron residents return home after Israeli military operation concludes
articles.title: Displaced in Hebron: Picking up pieces after Israeli siege
articles.summary: Palestinian families in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron began returning to their homes on Monday following a 10-day Israeli military operation. According to the Hebron Governorate’s Support and Relief Committee, approximately 3,300 people from 537 families were displaced during the security restrictions that affected several local neighborhoods.
articles.description: Displaced Hebron families return to damaged homes, left to pick up scattered pieces of their lives after Israeli siege.

articles.headline: Bharatiya Janata Party announces state-wide youth outreach campaign starting November 9
articles.title: BJP plans ‘Save Democracy, Eradicate Anarchy’ campaign starting Nov. 9
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party MLA V. Sunil Kumar announced a youth outreach campaign titled Prajaprabhutva ulisi, aarajakathe alisi, running across 500 locations from November 9 to 30. During a press conference, Mr. Kumar criticized the Congress government over electoral roll revisions, delayed milk subsidies, and drought relief conditions, while demanding a transparent investigation into a recent sting operation.
articles.description: BJP MLA Sunil Kumar accuses the Congress of misleading people by selectively questioning the credibility of EVMs, raising objections to SIR

articles.headline: Karnataka High Court declares cross-border police operation by Maharashtra personnel illegal
articles.title: Deepfakes, impersonation of probe agencies call for verified inter-State police operations, says Karnataka HC
articles.summary: The High Court of Karnataka ruled that an investigative operation conducted by Maharashtra police at tobacco firms in Tumakuru was illegal for failing to coordinate with local authorities. Justice Suraj Govindaraj emphasized that rising cyber fraud and deepfakes necessitate strict verification during inter-state police operations to prevent intimidation by potential imposters. While declaring the local inspection invalid, the court declined to quash the underlying criminal case.
articles.description: Finds Maharashtra police action in Karnataka without informing local police illegal

articles.headline: Prakasam district administration prepares precautions as Cyclone Murasu approaches
articles.title: Prakasam district on high alert as Murasu cyclone approaches
articles.summary: Prakasam district authorities accelerated preparations for Cyclone Murasu on November 2, 2026, identifying twenty-six vulnerable villages and establishing seventy relief centres. Special officer Ranjit Basha and Collector P. Rajababu directed officials to evacuate vulnerable residents, deploy disaster response teams, and arrange emergency supplies to minimize potential damage from strong winds.

articles.headline: Telangana Congress mobilises thousands of party workers for Delhi public meeting
articles.title: Telangana Congress showcases its might in Delhi rally with massive participation
articles.summary: The Telangana Congress mobilised over fifteen thousand leaders and supporters for an opposition public meeting in New Delhi on November 2, 2026. Despite railway authorities declining special train permissions, Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee president B. Mahesh Kumar Goud arranged alternative transport using over one hundred buses and private vehicles to demonstrate the party organizational strength.
articles.description: CM Revanth and PCC president Mahesh Goud made it possible with minute preparations

articles.headline: Foreign secretary Vikram Misri attributes Chinese harshness to pandemic stigma
articles.title: Global criticism during COVID-19 hardened China’s attitude towards world: Foreign Secretary Misri
articles.summary: India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri stated on October 31, 2026, that global criticism and a sense of stigmatization during the COVID-19 pandemic caused China to adopt a harsh attitude toward the international community and enforce strict internal lockdowns. Speaking at the Iqwat Global Business Conclave, Misri reflected on his tenure as ambassador to China, recalling the immense challenges posed by bilateral stress, travel restrictions, and the 2020 Galwan Valley confrontation.
articles.description: Misri also recalled that he faced a major challenge during his posting in China as Ambassador, when India and China had an unprecedented confrontation in eastern Ladakh's Galwan Valley

articles.headline: Raptadu school chainsaw attack victim recovers as political leaders demand compensation
articles.title: Raptadu chainsaw attack victim shows signs of recovery; Jagan seeks ₹50 lakh compensation
articles.summary: Gopika, a Class X student injured in a chainsaw attack at a Zilla Parishad High School in Raptadu, is showing steady recovery at Manipal Hospital in Bengaluru. Human Resources Development and Information Technology Minister Nara Lokesh praised a classmate for intervening, while YSR Congress Party president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy demanded 50 lakh rupees in compensation for the victim's family.
articles.description: Doctors at Manipal Hospital in Bengaluru say the Class X girl is conscious and improving; Minister Nara Lokesh praises her friend Lakshmi for her bravery and the YSRCP chief demands accountability from the State government

articles.headline: What we know about latest efforts to end US war on Iran
articles.title: What we know about latest efforts to end US war on Iran
articles.description: The foreign ministers of the US and Iran say a diplomatic end to the war is still possible.

articles.headline: Serbian railway station canopy collapse ends ruling party rule
articles.title: Student List | The young Serb unrest
articles.summary: The collapse of a concrete canopy at the Novi Sad Railway station in Serbia killed sixteen people, including two young children. Widespread public outrage over allegations of corruption and government negligence in the recently reconstructed state-funded project ultimately brought an end to fourteen years of rule by the Serbian Progressive Party led by Aleksandar Vucic.
articles.description: Serbia’s student protesters, who built a blockade movement against corruption and political establishment, brought down the government of Aleksandar Vučić

articles.headline: Directorate General of Civil Aviation probes Belagavi trainer aircraft crash
articles.title: Directorate General of Civil Aviation probe into Belagavi trainer aircraft crash finds many deficiencies in training academy
articles.summary: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation released a report stating that Redbird Flight Training Academy suffered from maintenance and manpower deficiencies during a 2023 crash. A student pilot executing a solo flight near Belagavi Airport experienced engine failure and forced a landing after using unauthorized fuel. The aircraft sustained heavy damage, though the pilot remained uninjured.
articles.description: On May 30, 2023, a 24-year-old student trainee pilot flying a TECNAM P2008JC aircraft was involved in a forced landing incident near Belagavi Airport while conducting a solo circuit and landing exercise.

articles.headline: Natural rubber price reaches a historic milestone of 300 rupees
articles.title: Rubber price touches record ₹300 a kg
articles.summary: Domestic natural rubber prices touched three hundred rupees per kilogram for the first time on Monday according to Rubber Board data. Officials attributed the rally to tight domestic supplies driven by El Nino and international energy pressures. The Union Commerce Ministry announced plans to include Keralam in upcoming plantation programs to boost regional production.
articles.description: Sharp rise in rubber prices is attributed to a combination of factors, including tight domestic supplies, low rubber production across Southeast Asian countries due to climatic factors, conflict in West Asia affecting synthetic rubber production. Centre plans to include Keralam in the second phase of ATMA’s plantation programme to boost local output.

articles.headline: Chief Minister announces new women's policy implementation without compromises
articles.title: Women’s policy will be implemented without compromises: CM
articles.summary: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan announced that a model women policy ensuring socio-economic development and safety will be implemented without compromises. Speaking at Her Summit 2026, he outlined plans for a special law against cyberattacks and initiatives for financial independence. Minister Bindhu Krishna added that the framework will focus on gender equality and entrepreneurship support.
articles.description: Says government mulling special Act to prevent cyber attacks on women; inaugurates Her Summit 2026 organised by Women and Child Development department for framing new women’s policy

articles.headline: Lula da Silva wins historic Brazilian presidential runoff election
articles.title: Lula da Silva | The Pele of Brazil’s politics
articles.summary: Lula da Silva made history by becoming the first Brazilian president to finish second in the initial election round and subsequently win the presidential runoff. During the campaign, opponent Flavio Bolsonaro weaponized an old injury involving da Silva losing a finger while working in a factory, prompting a sharp response from the Workers Party leader.
articles.description: The left-wing leader’s victory in Brazil, after finishing second in the first round, reflects the deep roots of the Workers’ Party, which built its support base through resistance to the military dictatorship in the early 1980s, as well as the declining appeal of Bolsonarismo

articles.headline: Israeli Arab parties set to back Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc
articles.title: Arab parties back Eisenkot: What’s the latest in Israel’s coalition talks?
articles.summary: Israel Arab parties winning nineteen seats are set to back opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, complicating Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu efforts to form a government. The Jewish opposition bloc fell short of a majority, while Arab factions like Raam and the Joint List offered outside support to oust Netanyahu despite facing political friction and ongoing election investigations.
articles.description: Political wrangling is still ongoing as all blocs weigh potential paths to power.

articles.headline: Barcelona face Aston Villa in UEFA Champions League matchday four
articles.title: Barcelona vs Aston Villa: Champions League – Predictions, news, lineups
articles.summary: Aston Villa seek to extend their perfect start in the UEFA Champions League with a match against Barcelona on Tuesday, November 2, at Spotify Camp Nou. Barcelona sit top of La Liga but are eighth in the European standings after losing to Paris Saint-Germain. Meanwhile, Unai Emery’s side aim to continue their strong continental campaign following domestic successes and recent legal action involving pundit Jamie Carragher.
articles.description: Aston Villa, second in the UEFA Champions League table after three wins from three, head to Barcelona, three points back

articles.headline: Three BSF personnel and civilian injured in Tripura border clash
articles.title: Three BSF personnel, a civilian injured in Tripura clash
articles.summary: Three Border Security Force personnel and a local youth sustained injuries during a clash in the Sepahijala district of Tripura on November 2, 2026. The confrontation erupted when residents protested the detention of a youth, leading to a road blockade and brawl. Police deployed armed personnel to restore normalcy while investigating the incident.
articles.description: The clash occurred during a road blockade by locals protesting against the detention and assault of a youth

articles.headline: U.S. President Donald Trump delays decision on fresh Iran strikes
articles.title: Rubio says U.S. yet to decide on new Iran strikes
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump has not yet decided on launching new military strikes against Iran amid stalled peace talks, according to Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Speaking on Saturday in Atlanta, Georgia, Rubio stated that the administration remains open to a diplomatic solution despite ongoing tensions and Iranian targeting of commercial vessels.
articles.description: Iran’s supreme leader October 31, 2026 warned the United States and Israel against launching new attacks, following threats to resume strikes after crucial elections

articles.headline: Centre notifies grievance redressal rules for VB-G RAM G scheme
articles.title: VB-G RAM G grievances must be resolved in 15 days under new rules; no FIR clause
articles.summary: The Indian Ministry of Rural Development notified new grievance redressal rules for the Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission on November 2, 2026, mandating a 15-day resolution window for complaints. The final framework dropped several draft provisions, including mandatory first information report filings for financial irregularities, while introducing digital tracking and multiple submission channels.
articles.description: Two key clauses that were in the grievance redressal rules under MGNREGA were not included: requirement for FIR registration in cases of prima facie evidence of financial irregularities, and for action-taken reports on grievances to be placed before panchayat and district panchayat meetings

articles.headline: Karnataka Examination Authority introduces single examination system for 5,431 departmental posts
articles.title: Karnataka Examination Authority to conduct single examination for recruitment to multiple posts
articles.summary: The Karnataka Examination Authority has initiated a single recruitment examination process for 5,431 vacancies across 33 departments. According to Executive Director H. Prasanna, the new system allows candidates to apply for multiple posts using one application and fee, reducing delays and financial burdens. Selections will be determined through merit, reservation categories, and candidate preference counselling resembling professional course admissions.
articles.description: Recruitment through a CET-style counselling process; KEA will conduct a common examination for equivalent posts across 33 departments at once

articles.headline: Disadvantaged mother carries sick daughter across flooded terrain in S. Kota
articles.title: Tribal hamlet cut off from mainland forces woman carry sick daughter for treatment
articles.summary: A 36-year-old tribal woman named Sunkaramma carried her 11-year-old sick daughter Sampoorna for seven kilometres across hilly terrain in S. Kota due to a lack of transport after Cyclone Arnab damaged road connectivity. District Collector S. Ramsundar Reddy instructed officials to investigate the incident and ensure motorable road repairs following treatment at the S. Kota government hospital.

articles.headline: National Conference leadership negotiates with disgruntled legislators demanding internal reforms
articles.title: Top NC leaders reach out to disgruntled lawmakers in Jammu and Kashmir
articles.summary: The ruling National Conference in Jammu and Kashmir dispatched senior leaders, including Ali Muhammad Sagar, to meet roughly 20 dissident legislators following a meeting at lawmaker Qaiser Jamsheed Lone's residence on October 27. The dissenting members submitted a ten-point memorandum demanding internal party restructuring, the restoration of statehood, and policy changes to address grievances regarding administrative leadership.
articles.description: Around 20 legislators who raised the banner of dissension over the party functioning and certain leaders close to Chief Minister Omar Abdullah have put forth 10-point demands to “restructure the party”

articles.headline: Texas Muslims focus on local stakes amid rising midterm election Islamophobia
articles.title: As Islamophobia ramps up in US midterms, Texas Muslims eye local stakes
articles.summary: Muslim voters in Texas face escalating Islamophobia during the final stretch of the midterm elections as state Republican leaders target Islamic customs and push policies against Sharia law. Accounting for less than two percent of the population, community organisers in Houston and across the state have significantly expanded voter registration drives to counter political marginalisation and demand representation.
articles.description: Texas Muslims grapple with a slate of policies they say stigmatise their community, push for change at the ballot box.

articles.headline: Supreme Court dismisses government challenge against Vedanta arbitration awards
articles.title: Supreme Court raps Centre for stalling enforcement of Vedanta arbitration awards
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed the Union government challenge against a Delhi High Court order that allowed mining major Vedanta Ltd. and Ravva Oil Singapore Pte. Ltd. to enforce foreign arbitration awards totaling nearly $99 million. A Bench questioned the resistance from the Centre, warning that prolonged legal delays could undermine India status as an international arbitration hub. The underlying dispute originated from a 1994 production-sharing contract for the Ravva oilfield.
articles.description: Bench dismisses Union government’s challenge to a Delhi High Court order allowing Vedanta Ltd. and Ravva Oil (Singapore) Pte. Ltd. to enforce foreign arbitration awards involving claims of nearly $99 million

articles.headline: Wizz Air flight escorted by Hungarian fighter jet after bomb threat
articles.title: Wizz Air flight from Luton in emergency landing after bomb threat
articles.summary: A Wizz Air flight travelling from London Luton Airport to Sofia was escorted by a Hungarian military fighter jet to Budapest following a mid-air bomb threat. The aircraft made a safe emergency landing at Budapest Liszt Ferenc International Airport, where security authorities conducted thorough inspections of the passengers and plane. Wizz Air confirmed that nothing suspicious was found during the checks and the aircraft prepared to resume its journey.
articles.description: A Hungarian fighter jet escorted the aircraft to Budapest after the threat was received mid-air.

articles.headline: Ukraine air raid app hacked to display false radiation and attack threats
articles.title: Fake nuclear warnings issued after Ukrainian and Russian air alert apps hacked
articles.summary: Ukraine’s Air Alert application was compromised on Sunday, sending false notifications of radiation, chemical, and street fighting threats in Kyiv. The Ukrainian Air Force and Central Intelligence Agency confirmed the cyber-attack and stated there was no actual danger. Officials across multiple regions urged citizens to rely on verified sources while the ministry addressed the technical failure.
articles.description: Neither government has confirmed who was responsible for the cyberattacks on Sunday evening.

articles.headline: Eight-year-old boy suspended and evaluated after assaulting six-year-old girl
articles.title: Shock and anger in India after eight-year-old beats six-year-old in classroom
articles.summary: Public outrage emerged across India following viral CCTV footage from a government school in Panchkula, Haryana, showing an eight-year-old boy severely assaulting a six-year-old girl on October 28. The victim received critical injuries and is recovering at PGIMER hospital in Chandigarh. Police registered a case against the school management for negligence, while the boy was placed in a juvenile observation home for psychiatric evaluation.
articles.description: The girl, who was seriously injured, is out of danger, but remains traumatised by her assault, her family said.

articles.headline: FBI links North Korea to record crypto heist
articles.title: FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3bn crypto heist from Binance
articles.summary: The Federal Bureau of Investigation has attributed the theft of six point three billion dollars in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance to North Korea. Authorities stated the hackers laundered funds by converting them into Ethereum. Meanwhile, Binance replaced ninety percent of the stolen amount using internal funds and its Secure Asset Fund for Users reserve to protect customers.
articles.description: Crypto firm Binance says it has covered 90 percent of losses from the multibillion-dollar hack.

articles.headline: What we know about the alert app hack in Ukraine and Russia
articles.title: What we know about the alert app hack in Ukraine and Russia
articles.description: Both Ukraine and Russia say their air raid alert apps were cyber-attacked - Joe Tidy explains what we know so far.

articles.headline: Granules India reports 39 percent increase in quarterly net profit
articles.title: Granules India net profit rises 39% to ₹182 cr on higher revenue
articles.summary: Indian drugmaker Granules India posted a 39 percent year-on-year jump in consolidated net profit to ₹181.8 crore for the September quarter, driven by a 20 percent rise in revenue from operations to ₹1,559.9 crore. Chairman and Managing Director Krishna Prasad Chigurupati noted that EBITDA reached ₹338 crore despite rising input and logistics expenses stemming from tensions in West Asia. He also addressed ongoing U.S. FDA inspections at the company Gagillapur facility.
articles.description: Revenue crosses ₹1,500 crore despite higher input and logistics costs driven by West Asia tensions, expect cost pressures to persist, says CMD Chigurupati

articles.headline: Thousands in Israel urge Eisenkot-Arab deal
articles.title: Thousands rally in Israel urging ‘Jewish-Arab’ coalition to oust Netanyahu
articles.summary: Thousands of demonstrators gathered in Tel Aviv to pressure opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot into forming a coalition with Arab parties to unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Following an election deadlock where Netanyahu and Eisenkot fell short of a majority, Arab-led parties secured nineteen seats, creating a potential path to a sixty-seven seat majority government.
articles.description: In a counterprotest, Netanyahu supporters demand that Israel should not have a government with 'terrorists'.

articles.headline: Three killed in Manipur gunfight
articles.title: 3 killed in gunfight between rival groups in Manipur's Noney
articles.summary: Three individuals belonging to the Kuki community died during a multi-hour gunfight between rival armed groups in Manipur's Noney district. The clash erupted at Kekru Naga village, prompting police to implement security measures. The Kuki Inpi Manipur apex body strongly condemned the killings and alleged that Naga militant groups were responsible for the violent incident.
articles.description: Meanwhile, the Kuki Inpi Manipur (KIM), the apex body of the Kuki community, strongly condemned the killing of the three youths

articles.headline: Neocloud firms spark AI bubble fears
articles.title: These firms you've never heard of are feeding fears the AI bubble could burst
articles.summary: Neocloud data centre companies like CoreWeave and Nebius are facing investor scrutiny over heavy debt loads and financial stability as artificial intelligence spending forecasts fluctuate. Industry analysts warn that many independent operators could face acquisition or closure amid rising interest rates and heavy hardware costs, though demand for computing power from major artificial intelligence developers remains high.
articles.description: The amount of debt held by data centres is measured in the tens of billions of pounds.

articles.headline: HPE recommends measuring cost per merged pull request for AI coding
articles.title: Stop counting tokens, start counting what ships
articles.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise advises software developers to track cost per merged pull request rather than counting tokens to evaluate artificial intelligence investments accurately. According to the company, hybrid platforms routing routine tasks to on-premises open-weight models can reduce token costs by thirty to fifty percent while maintaining control over sensitive proprietary code repositories.
articles.description: When a developer gives an AI agent a coding task, the agent does more than answer once. It plans, generates code, runs tests, and repeats the process to correct errors. A single task can use 10 to 50 times more tokens than a basic chat prompt. The more useful the agent becomes, the more calls…

articles.headline: Vultr launches 20-megawatt AI supercluster in Chennai using AMD GPUs
articles.title: Vultr launches 20-MW AI supercluster in Chennai; aims 1 GW capacity by 2029
articles.summary: Cloud infrastructure provider Vultr announced the deployment of a twenty-megawatt artificial intelligence supercluster in Chennai, India, utilizing Advanced Micro Devices Instinct graphics processing units. General Manager Amit Rai stated the company aims to achieve six hundred megawatts of capacity by 2028 and gigawatt scale by 2029 to serve global enterprises, startups, and research institutions.
articles.description: The facility is expected to house around 10,000 GPUs initially. Global enterprises have pre-reserved a large portion of its capacity, the company said

articles.headline: Student movements and youth turnout unseat leaders in Serbia and Hungary
articles.title: How the downfall of Serbia's Vučiċ mirrored that of Hungary's Orbán
articles.summary: Popular movements led by tech-savvy youth ousted long-serving leaders Viktor Orbán in Hungary and Aleksandar Vučić in Serbia after record turnouts of 79 percent and 69 percent respectively. Digital monitoring tools and cross-border cooperation helped detect electoral fraud. Both former leaders now face potential corruption prosecution following parallel political downfalls driven by public discontent.
articles.description: Defeat for Serbia's Aleksandar Vučiċ in last weekend's vote was a carbon copy of Viktor Orbán's fall in Hungary.

articles.headline: Jordanian King Abdullah vows firm response following Karak church attack
articles.title: Jordan’s King Abdullah promises to confront ‘terrorists’ after Karak attack
articles.summary: King Abdullah II of Jordan addressed parliament in Amman following a deadly church attack in Karak that killed nine people, pledging that the state will confront terrorism decisively. During his opening speech, the monarch also warned that Israeli expansionism poses the greatest threat to regional security and emphasized the protection of national water supplies.
articles.description: King tells parliament attackers ‘are not of us’ and warns that Israeli expansionism is greatest threat to the region.

articles.headline: Federal judge blocks Trump administration from threatening election officials
articles.title: Judge orders Trump administration to stop threatening US election officials
articles.summary: United States District Judge Trina Thompson ordered the federal government to halt threats of criminal charges against local and state election officials processing ballots. The Department of Justice previously demanded officials set aside thousands of voter ballots allegedly cast by non-citizens. Civil rights groups filed a legal complaint challenging the administration actions ahead of elections.
articles.description: The order comes after election officials received letters demanding they set aside the ballots of possible non-citizen voters.

articles.headline: Gen Z-led protests in Germany turn violent
articles.title: Gen Z-led protests in Germany turn violent
articles.description: Protesters clashed with police as thousands took to the streets across 34 cities in Germany.

articles.headline: IndiGo CEO Willie Walsh outlines market opportunities amid challenging industry conditions
articles.title: IndiGo expects to see flight capacity growth in Q3 despite elevated jet fuel prices
articles.summary: During his first in-person briefing on November 2, 2026, IndiGo Chief Executive Officer Willie Walsh stated that the airline sees significant growth prospects despite challenging industry conditions driven by rising fuel costs and rupee depreciation. Walsh noted that IndiGo expects to receive wide-body Airbus A350 aircraft starting in the second quarter of 2028 and views the new Navi Mumbai airport as a major opportunity.
articles.description: At his first in-person briefing after taking charge as CEO in August, Mr. Walsh said the airline expects to start getting the wide-body A350 aircraft from the second quarter of 2028

articles.headline: Ryanair considers wage freeze and fare hikes amid rising fuel costs
articles.title: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
articles.summary: Irish carrier Ryanair is weighing temporary pay freezes for staff and higher European airfares to offset surging fuel costs. The airline reported a sixteen percent drop in pre-tax profits to two point four billion euros during the six months ending in September, driven by aviation fuel price spikes following the war in the Middle East involving the United States, Israel, and Iran.
articles.description: The airline says fuel prices may rise by €2bn in 2028 unless there is an end to the US-Israel war with Iran.

articles.headline: Yemeni government forces advance against Houthis in Al-Jawf governorate
articles.title: Al-Jawf becomes new hotspot in Yemen war between government forces, Houthis
articles.summary: Yemeni government troops captured the Huwaishan mountain range in Al-Jawf governorate as part of Operation Dawn of Yemen to regain territory from Houthi forces. Field commander Colonel Rabie Al-Qurashi stated the advance disrupts rebel supply routes and increases pressure on Houthi positions near the provincial capital of al-Hazm.
articles.description: Recent military advances by Yemeni government forces highlight the geographic and strategic significance of Al-Jawf.

articles.headline: Suspected cyberattacks cause overnight temperature spikes in European supermarket refrigeration
articles.title: Suspected cyberattacks trigger supermarket fridge failures across Europe
articles.summary: Supermarket refrigeration systems experienced unauthorized temperature increases across Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Luxembourg, and Sweden following suspected cyberattacks. Retailers and officials reported that units were switched to defrost mode or elevated to fifty degrees Celsius, prompting European food and agriculture commissioner Christophe Hansen to condemn the incidents as deliberate disruption attempts.
articles.description: Temperature increases have been reported in dozens of store cooling systems , weeks after a similar attack in France.

articles.headline: Uganda begins troop withdrawal from Somalia after twenty years
articles.title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years
articles.summary: Uganda started withdrawing Uganda People's Defence Forces troops from Mogadishu, handing security responsibilities to Somali forces. The phased withdrawal follows two decades of military involvement combating al-Shabab. Uganda plans to complete the transition by August 2027, though troops under separate bilateral security arrangements will remain in the country.
articles.description: Uganda has been helping Somalia battle an insurgency led by the al-Shabab militant group since 2007.

articles.headline: Indian stock indices surge nearly two percent driven by strong corporate earnings
articles.title: Indices end nearly 2% higher on Monday, RIL posts best gains since 2020
articles.summary: Benchmark indices extended a three-day winning streak on November 2, 2026, as the Sensex gained 1,233 points to close at 75,682.78 and the Nifty 50 rose 387.70 points to 23,440. Reliance Industries led the rally with an 11.6 percent jump following a 32 percent increase in second-quarter profit to 29,250 crore rupees. Meanwhile, Brent crude prices declined by over four percent amid geopolitical developments, supporting investor sentiment across major sectors.
articles.description: Reliance Industries marked its highest level since over six years and jumped 11.6% following a higher-than-expected earnings for Q2FY27

articles.headline: No-cost Equated Monthly Instalments conceal hidden interest charges and inflated purchase prices.
articles.title: No-cost EMI: a loan that is portrayed as free
articles.summary: Financial institutions and retailers market festive zero-cost instalment plans to consumers purchasing high-value electronics and home appliances. According to reports published on November 2, 2026, lenders recover financing charges by either inflating product prices or forfeiting standard cash discounts. This practice matters because buyers ultimately finance their own interest payments rather than receiving genuinely free credit.
articles.description: A ₹60,000 phone, 6 easy instalments of ₹10,000, no interest. It feels as if the shopkeeper has done you a favour. He has not. Nobody lends money for free and nobody sells at a loss. Someone pays.

articles.headline: Can Americans who disagree on politics still find common ground?
articles.title: Can Americans who disagree on politics still find common ground?
articles.description: As Michigan's Senate race exposes deep divisions, Al Jazeera speaks to four voters with opposing political views.

articles.headline: Supreme Court declines urgent plea against airfare hikes in India
articles.title: Don't travel by air, says Supreme Court; refuses urgent listing of plea alleging 700% hike in airfares
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India refused an urgent hearing on November 2, 2026, regarding a petition alleging a nearly 700 percent increase in aviation fares, telling the advocate to avoid air travel. Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta, and Aparesh Kumar Singh presided over the matter. The court is already reviewing a separate petition concerning unpredictable airfare fluctuations and regulatory transparency in the civil aviation sector.
articles.description: Centre says aviation rules under Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam being fast-tracked to curb volatility and ensure passenger protection

articles.headline: Mehbooba Mufti urges Centre to resolve Kashmir through dialogue
articles.title: Kashmir issue will be resolved by talks that heal, not experiments or UAPA: Mehbooba Mufti
articles.summary: Former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Mehbooba Mufti urged the central government on November 2, 2026, to abandon restrictive measures like the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act and initiate healing talks instead. Speaking at a workers convention in Srinagar, the Peoples Democratic Party president criticized ongoing security crackdowns, employee terminations, and political duplicity. She also called for reopening traditional trade routes across borders.
articles.description: The Government of India experimented a lot to enforce peace in Kashmir; the baton policy will not work...This year, the protesters in Delhi tasted what Kashmir has been suffering all these years. Mehbooba Mufti says

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh chief minister directs officials to prepare for cyclone floods
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: CM directs officials to brace for flood into Bapatla district
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu instructed district administrations on November 2, 2026, to execute precautionary measures ahead of Cyclone Murasu. During a video conference with Bapatla Collector Vinod Kumar V, the Chief Minister warned of severe flood inflows through irrigation canals from upstream districts. Educational institutions in Bapatla were ordered closed for two days to ensure student safety amidst heavy rain forecasts.
articles.description: Heavy inflows are expected through irrigation canals from upstream districts for four days

articles.headline: University of California researchers develop light-based technique to detect deepfakes
articles.title: New technique uses light to spot deepfakes in seconds
articles.summary: Researchers at the University of California, Los Angeles, developed a new laboratory technique that uses video lighting analysis to successfully identify deepfake videos. Published on November 3, 2026, the method addresses human limitations, as research shows people correctly identify manipulated media only half the time.
articles.description: In tests, the system was able to identify manipulated videos with an accuracy of 99.86% and real videos with an accuracy of 95.72% — while processing 15 videos at a time

articles.headline: India Meteorological Department issues severe weather alerts for five Telangana districts
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: Red alert in two Telangana districts, orange in three more on November 3
articles.summary: Authorities have placed multiple regions on high alert as Cyclone Murasu approaches the Andhra Pradesh coast. The India Meteorological Department announced red alerts for Nalgonda and Nagarkurnool alongside orange warnings for three neighboring areas on November 3, 2026. Heavy rainfall and thunderstorms are anticipated to impact local communities during this period according to the latest official bulletin.

articles.headline: Cyclone Murasu leads to flight cancellations and school closures in Chennai
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: List of flights cancelled to and from Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada
articles.summary: Cyclone Murasu intensified into a severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal, resulting in flight cancellations at Chennai International Airport and school closures in Chennai and Tiruvallur districts on November 2, 2026. The India Meteorological Department stated the storm is expected to cross the South Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur with high wind speeds.
articles.description: Cyclone Murasu comes just days after Cyclone Arnab made landfall in Andhra Pradesh on October 27,2026.

articles.headline: Judge dismisses Donald Trump defamation lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal
articles.title: Trump loses legal battle over Epstein-linked Wall Street Journal case
articles.summary: United States District Judge Darrin Gayles permanently dismissed Donald Trump's ten billion dollar defamation lawsuit against Rupert Murdoch and The Wall Street Journal. The judge concluded that the president failed to establish actual malice regarding an article that linked him to Jeffrey Epstein. Filed in Miami on July 18, 2025, the complaint contested coverage of a 2003 birthday note.
articles.description: Judge permanently drops Trump's $10bn WSJ lawsuit, ruling he failed to prove actual malice in the newspaper's reporting.

articles.headline: Turkiye transfers jailed Kurdistan Workers’ Party founder to new facility
articles.title: Jailed PKK founder Ocalan moved to new section of Turkish island prison
articles.summary: Legislators confirmed that Abdullah Ocalan has been relocated to a newly constructed section on Imrali island after spending twenty-seven years in detention. Political representatives urged Ankara to revitalize peace discussions following the transfer. The long-running conflict involving the armed group and the state has resulted in significant casualties since nineteen eighty-four.
articles.description: Improving prison conditions for Abdullah Ocalan has been a key Kurdish demand in push to end PKK-Turkiye conflict.

articles.headline: Aligarh Muslim University holds first student union elections in eight years
articles.title: AMU wants women on campus, not at the ballot box
articles.summary: Aligarh Muslim University in India has launched its first student union elections in eight years. Male candidates wearing traditional black sherwanis campaigned on campus lawns for the Aligarh Muslim University Students Union vote. During campaigning, female students questioned candidates regarding their exclusion from voting rights at the university ballot box.
articles.description: Around 4,000 women students at AMU’s Women’s College have been denied voting rights in the Aligarh Muslim University Students’ Union (AMUSU) elections, raising concerns over gender discrimination and unequal representation. Their fight to be included in the university-wide electoral process has brought renewed scrutiny to the separate-union rules and the barriers women face in campus politics, finds A. M. Jigeesh

articles.headline: YSRCP leader accuses election commission of complicity in civic poll malpractices
articles.title: Jagan accuses SEC of complicity in civic poll malpractices, says YSRCP will go to court
articles.summary: YSR Congress Party president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy accused the State Election Commission of enabling electoral malpractices during municipal elections. He claimed officials and police facilitated booth capturing, rigging, and violence, particularly in Pulivendula. Despite overwhelming evidence, the commission ordered repolling in only four booths, prompting the opposition party to launch a legal battle against the irregularities.
articles.description: The SEC ordered repolling in only four booths despite “overwhelming evidence”, the YSRCP president alleges

articles.headline: Kimi Antonelli secures Formula One world championship at Mexico City Grand Prix
articles.title: ‘Just the beginning’ for Antonelli, F1’s prodigious, charismatic new king
articles.summary: The twenty-year-old driver achieved a historic milestone by clinching the world title for Mercedes on Sunday. Finishing behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, the Italian competitor became the youngest champion in the sport's history. Tributes poured in from international figures and racing engineers celebrating the exceptional achievement achieved during the recent competition.
articles.description: Kimi Antonelli, F1’s youngest world champion at 20, has become the life and soul of the paddock with his personality.

articles.headline: Keralam court sentences former hospital superintendent to 20 years in prison.
articles.title: 78-year-old paediatrician sentenced to 47 years in POCSO case in Keralam
articles.summary: Dr P Krishnan, a 78-year-old paediatrician and former superintendent of the Kasaragod District Hospital, received a total 47-year sentence, running concurrently to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment, after being found guilty under the Indian Penal Code and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. Judge PM Suresh imposed a fine of ₹1.25 lakh for the 2020 assault on a 15-year-old girl in Periya.
articles.description: The court awarded 20 years of rigorous imprisonment to the accused under Section 376(3) of the IPC for raping a girl below 16 years of age. He was also sentenced to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment under Sections 6(1) and 5(e) of the POCSO Act.

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts missile as clashes escalate across Yemen
articles.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts a missile as fighting rages in Yemen’s al-Jawf
articles.summary: Air defences successfully destroyed a ballistic missile targeting the southern region of Saudi Arabia amid ongoing military confrontations. Meanwhile, government forces continued operations against Houthi fighters in al-Jawf to regain strategic territory. Humanitarian concerns intensified as vital supply routes remained blocked, severely disrupting health facilities and daily life for residents across the affected areas.
articles.description: Houthi-affiliated media report that seven people were wounded in strikes on the city of Hodeidah.

articles.headline: Autonomous artificial intelligence agents transform navigation across the internet
articles.title: The agentic web is here
articles.summary: Advanced large language models are successfully realizing early visions of automated web navigation through software tools like Muse and Claude Duet. These intelligent systems interact with online services and process data rapidly without requiring specialized manual tags. Technology experts note this transition marks a major shift toward an agentic web that will fundamentally alter human internet experiences.
articles.description: In 2001, a decade after he invented the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee articulated a new vision. Together with two colleagues, he published an article in the magazine Scientific American in which he outlined what he called the “Semantic Web”: an internet designed to be navigated by autonomous software agents that could address our every…

articles.headline: Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe
articles.title: Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe
articles.description: More than 320,000 people demonstrated across France against the rising cost of living and poor public services, with clashes between some protesters and police.

articles.headline: Pakistan deploys over eight thousand police personnel to protect anti-polio vaccination teams in Karachi
articles.title: Over 8,000 police personnel deployed to protect polio teams in Pakistan's Karachi
articles.summary: More than 8,000 police personnel were deployed in Karachi on Monday to secure vaccination teams during a week-long anti-polio campaign running through November 8. Karachi Commissioner Syed Hassan Naqvi stated security has been heavily prioritised following past attacks and resistance from community members. Pakistan and Afghanistan remain the only two countries globally where polio is still endemic, according to the World Health Organisation.
articles.description: The development comes a day after the National Emergency Operations Centre for Polio Eradication confirmed that the new case was reported from Khyber district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province

articles.headline: Milky Way grew by consuming nearby galaxies and leaving stellar streams
articles.title: The Milky Way grew by devouring galaxies, leaving a trail of ghost stars
articles.summary: Galactic archaeologists studying stellar ages, chemical compositions, and motions discovered that the Milky Way expanded over nearly 12 billion years by devouring smaller galaxies like the Magellanic clouds. These violent collisions rip apart smaller galaxies, leaving behind distinct stellar streams that reveal the evolutionary history of our galaxy.
articles.description: Galactic archaeologists are using precise measures and larger sample sizes afforded by new missions to tease apart minute differences between groups of stars, revealing the history of the Milky Way going back almost 12 billion years

articles.headline: Democratic leaders rally around Abdul El-Sayed after Michigan endorsement fallout
articles.title: US midterms: 1 day to go – Democrats rally around El-Sayed amid attacks
articles.summary: Democratic leaders condemned Representative Haley Stevens for endorsing Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers over Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan. The dispute emerged ahead of Tuesday midterm elections. Meanwhile, a federal judge dismissed a Trump administration lawsuit seeking to block certification in Alaska, and early voting surged across several states involving millions of registered voters.
articles.description: Democrats slam Haley Stevens over her endorsement of a Republican candidate a day before the polls.

articles.headline: Former Cleveland Guardians pitchers face MLB spot-fixing trial in New York
articles.title: MLB ‘spot-fixing’ trial set to begin in US court
articles.summary: Former Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz went on trial in Brooklyn federal court on bribery and wire fraud conspiracy charges. Prosecutors alleged the players accepted payoffs to provide gamblers with information on pitches. Both pleaded not guilty and face a jury trial expected to last a month.
articles.description: MLB pitchers charged with conspiracy to influence sporting contests by bribery go on trial in New York.

articles.headline: Anthrax outbreak kills twenty-eight hippopotamuses in Virunga National Park
articles.title: Anthrax outbreak kills hippos in DR Congo’s Virunga National Park
articles.summary: Laboratory tests confirmed an anthrax outbreak caused the deaths of twenty-eight hippopotamuses in Virunga National Park over a one-month period. Carcasses were discovered in the Semuliki River in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Park officials and experts warned that the bacteria can transmit to humans, prompting heightened surveillance and community warnings.
articles.description: Drought and conflict compound the threat to wildlife in eastern DR Congo.

articles.headline: Sydney deploys heavily armed police unit after Bondi attack
articles.title: Sydney deploys heavily armed police unit after Bondi attack
articles.description: Sydney deploys heavily armed police unit after Bondi attack

articles.headline: Two men arrested in Telangana following a murder and robbery
articles.title: Murder-robbery cracked within three hours, two held in Telangana’s Nirmal while fleeing in SUV
articles.summary: Police in Telangana arrested two men within three hours of a murder and robbery in Choutuppal. The suspects were intercepted at the Ganjal Toll Plaza in Nirmal district after fleeing in a stolen Tata Safari. Authorities recovered over nine lakh rupees in cash alongside gold and silver ornaments, with the total seized property valued at over one crore rupees.
articles.description: Nephew spoke to the victim at 11 p.m., when the latter said two people came to meet him. Later, the nephew received two voice notes warning him to not report the murder, said Yadadri-Bhongir SP

articles.headline: Mahadev betting app promoter Sourabh Chandrakar extradited from Oman to India
articles.title: Mahadev betting syndicate ‘kingpin’ extradited from Oman
articles.summary: Sourabh Chandrakar, promoter of the illegal Mahadev Online Book betting app, was extradited to India from Oman on November 1, 2026, according to a Central Bureau of Investigation spokesperson. Located by the Royal Oman Police following an Interpol Red Corner Notice, Chandrakar faces charges in cases filed by the Central Bureau of Investigation and the Enforcement Directorate regarding an alleged 6,000-crore-rupee scam.
articles.description: CBI says it secured extradition of Sourabh Chandrakar, who had been arrested by police in Oman following an Interpol Red Corner Notice

articles.headline: Exam system flaws resemble Soviet shoe factories
articles.title: What India’s leaky exam system can learn from Soviet shoe factories
articles.summary: Recent protests and legal challenges regarding leaked examination papers highlight ongoing vulnerabilities in India's testing systems without producing concrete preventive measures. The operational inefficiencies of testing authorities parallel Soviet-era shoe factories where lack of consumer demand incentives and rampant resource pilferage persisted without structural correction.
articles.description: Unless we treat the exams as the complex economic product they are, with knowledge dispersed among specialised professionals and each player acting in their own self-interest, and restructure the financial incentives at play, we will keep having protests and Cabinet reshuffles and Committee appointments

articles.headline: Supreme Court closes Ram Temple embezzlement petitions after charge sheet filing
articles.title: SC disposes of Ram Temple embezzlement petitions after Uttar Pradesh says charge sheet filed
articles.summary: The Supreme Court closed multiple pleas seeking a Central Bureau of Investigation probe into the Ram Temple donations embezzlement case. State authorities in Uttar Pradesh informed the bench that a special investigation team had already filed a charge sheet. The apex court permitted petitioners to assist the trial court as victims of crime given the public interest involved.
articles.description: The Supreme Court allowed petitioners, including Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Case Trust, Ajay Kumar Rai, Narendra Kumar Goswami and Sudhakar Singh, to assist the trial court in further proceedings

articles.headline: Two foreign nationals die in suspected swimming pool electrocution at Bengaluru hotel
articles.title: Death in swimming pool: how two foreigners were electrocuted in a Bengaluru five-star hotel | Explained
articles.summary: Two foreign nationals died from suspected electrocution in a third-floor swimming pool at Hotel Conrad in Bengaluru. The victims were identified as a German airline crew member and a Slovakian tourist. According to hospital statements and police reports, rescue efforts were also hindered by electrical current in the water until hotel staff shut off the power supply. The Electrical Inspectorate and Halasuru police are investigating the incident.
articles.description: The deaths raises serious questions about electrical safety standards, maintenance protocols, and emergency preparedness at swimming pools in general and luxury hotels

articles.headline: Erdogan and Zelenskyy push for Black Sea shipping security
articles.title: Turkiye’s Erdogan urges Russia and Ukraine to stop Black Sea attacks
articles.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan urged Russia and Ukraine to halt attacks on civilian ships in the Black Sea during a joint news conference in Istanbul. Erdogan and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy agreed to collaborate on establishing a new grain corridor through the waterway to restore safe navigation, address global food security threats, and revive diplomatic peace efforts.
articles.description: Turkish president hosts Zelenskyy in Istanbul as the two leaders agree to work on a new Black Sea grain corridor.

articles.headline: US midterm elections historically bring significant seat losses for the presidential party.
articles.title: How the president’s party has fared in every US midterm election since 1946
articles.summary: American voters head to the polls to decide control of Congress by electing 435 House and 35 Senate seats. Historical data shows the presidential party loses House seats in 18 out of 20 midterms since 1946, averaging a loss of 26 seats. While opposing majorities can block legislation or launch investigations, current dynamics require Democrats to gain three House and four Senate seats.
articles.description: Only twice in the past 20 midterms has the president’s party gained House seats. Polls suggest 2026 won’t be the third.

articles.headline: Australian author Craig Silvey sentenced to seven months imprisonment for exploitation offences.
articles.title: Popular Australian children's author jailed over child exploitation offences
articles.summary: Judge Hayley Cormann sentenced the 44-year-old father-of-three to seven months in jail, backdated to October 22, following his guilty plea for possessing and distributing child exploitation material. Police seized electronic devices during a January raid on his Western Australia home. Publishers have subsequently pulled his acclaimed works like Jasper Jones and Runt from shelves.
articles.description: The author of Jasper Jones and Runt pleaded guilty in May after police raided his home months earlier.

articles.headline: Bengaluru electoral rolls contain numerous errors and garbled character entries
articles.title: ‘Husband Husband’ to ‘????’ and ‘XXX’: After SIR, Bengaluru’s electoral rolls riddled with errors
articles.summary: Bengaluru final electoral rolls contain at least one thousand discrepancies, including garbled character strings, missing relative names, and misplaced email addresses. Officials attributed the errors to transliteration issues and software glitches during file conversion, while affected voters noted that they only discovered the mistakes by checking their house numbers.
articles.description: In some polling stations, large clusters of consecutive entries have names and their relatives’ details replaced by jumbled letters and symbols, leaving several entries unrecognisable.

articles.headline: Jammu and Kashmir National Conference faces rare internal upheaval
articles.title: Why Kashmir’s ruling party National Conference stares at a rare upheaval | Explained
articles.summary: At least 17 legislators from the ruling National Conference party in Jammu and Kashmir held a four-hour meeting at the residence of Qaiser Jamsheed Lone on October 30, 2026. Senior party members and loyalists of president Dr. Farooq Abdullah attended the gathering, publicly expressing displeasure over recent developments within the political organisation which has governed for four decades.
articles.description: Omar Abdullah announced the induction of four new faces into the Cabinet on October 27, and reshuffled the portfolios. The legislators accused the CM and his close confidants of eroding the culture of consultation in the party by imposing decisions from the top, causing a political upheaval

articles.headline: Congress demands cancellation of Arunachal Pradesh hydropower project and release of detained protesters.
articles.title: Congress demands scrapping of Siang hydropower project, release of arrested protesters
articles.summary: The Arunachal Pradesh Congress Committee urged authorities to abandon the 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, citing risks of ancestral land submergence and community displacement. In a statement, the party demanded the immediate release of arrested demonstrators, withdrawal of unlawful activities cases, and the revocation of employee suspensions following opposition from indigenous Adi communities.
articles.description: The Arunachal Pradesh Congress Committee urged indigenous organisations, student unions, youth groups, civil society organisations and traditional institutions to unite against the proposed project

articles.headline: Americans vote in mid-term elections amid Republican congressional control
articles.title: Trump and Republicans in for a drubbing in mid-terms
articles.summary: Americans are voting on Tuesday in mid-term elections midway through Donald Trump second presidential term. Republicans currently hold narrow majorities in both the House and the Senate, but recent polls indicate they risk losing control of both chambers. All four hundred thirty five House seats and thirty five Senate seats are being contested.
articles.description: A forecasting model suggests the Democrats could win 230 of 435 seats in the House and 18 of 35 seats being contested in the Senate

articles.headline: Sri Lankan Navy detains seven Indian fishermen near Katchatheevu islet
articles.title: Seven Indian fishermen from Rameswaram detained by Sri Lankan Navy near Katchatheevu
articles.summary: Sri Lankan naval personnel arrested seven fishermen from Tamil Nadu on November 1, 2026, accusing them of poaching in international waters. The individuals were operating between the Katchatheevu islet and Mannar North before being transported with their vessel to a naval port. Fisheries Department officials stated that the group had deployed following authorized permits issued ahead of the Deepavali festival.
articles.description: Fishermen leaders have condemned the arrest and urged the Central and State governments to secure their release at the earliest.

articles.headline: Bangladesh garment factories reopen following wage protests and industry disruptions
articles.title: Bangladesh garment factories reopen as wage protests keep industry on edge
articles.summary: Bangladesh garment factories resumed operations after demonstrations over wages disrupted manufacturing across several cities and affected nearly one million workers. The sector accounts for over 80 percent of export earnings.
